items.description: Leonida Is A Native PC Recompilation Of The Xbox Version Of Grand Theft Auto 6
items.readme:
Leonida

Grand Theft Auto VI (Xbox Series) running natively on Windows, built on your PC from your own copy.

Other languages | Status | How to build | How it works | Want to help? | Credits | License | Discord

Leonida is a static recompilation project. The Xbox Series CPU is x86-64 like a PC, so the game's code is loaded and run natively, and the console's system software is reimplemented. The console's precompiled RDNA2 GPU programs are translated to SPIR-V for Vulkan. The game's models, textures and audio are read from your package. All of this happens **on your PC, from your own copy of the game**. > [!IMPORTANT] > This repository **does not contain the game, keys or an executable**, and it does not explain how to get them. You > need your own copy, with its files already readable on disk. Nothing here decrypts or works around any protection. > Everything the build creates (the generated shaders, extracted assets, the runtime folder and your saves) comes > from your game and stays on your PC. Never share those files. Discord: https://discord.gg/rexed
## Project status **Early. The game does not boot yet.** Everything that can be done without the game's executable is in place, so work on booting can start as soon as one is available to a developer. | What | Status | |---|---| | Booting, story mode, anything playable | ❌ No | | Finding and checking your copy (Xbox Series 1.0.2.1) | ✅ Works | | Shaders: carve, unpack native RDNA2 code, disassemble | ✅ All 26,503 | | Shaders: RDNA2 → SPIR-V translation | ✅ **All 26,503 translated**: 2,236 VS, 12,101 PS, 2,689 CS, 9,282 mesh, 195 geometry, with a per-shader metadata index for pipeline creation. All 26,503 passed `spirv-val` in the [LLVM 23.1.5 Linux run at `c432cdc`](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida/issues/644#issuecomment-7072972586). A [full-corpus run at `43d4703`](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida/issues/881#issuecomment-7075507328) also validated all 26,503 after `dcd8ecf` fixed the SPIR-V ID bound; the intervening `dedd75c` run was 26,501. ⚠️ 23,841 are wave64 (the FSSM header's wave-size flag; [docs/design.md](docs/design.md), "Wave size"): exact on 64-wide subgroups (AMD). On 32-wide subgroups (NVIDIA, Intel), compute and mesh shaders are exact with wave64 emulation (`--wave64-emulate`, on by default there); cross-half wave ops in vertex, pixel and geometry shaders are still approximate | | Shaders: RDNA2 → SPIR-V translation | ✅ **26,503 / 26,503 translated**: 2,236 VS, 12,101 PS, 2,689 CS, 9,282 mesh, 195 geometry, with a per-shader metadata index for pipeline creation. The LLVM 23.1.5 Linux rerun at `c432cdc` and the LLVM 23.1.3 Windows rerun at `43d0015` both translated all 26,503 ([Linux](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida/issues/644#issuecomment-7072972586), [Windows](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida/issues/644#issuecomment-7074299915)). Translation and SPIR-V validation are separate steps; validation results are listed below. ⚠️ 21,545 are wave64: exact on 64-wide subgroups (AMD). On 32-wide subgroups (NVIDIA, Intel), compute and mesh shaders are exact with wave64 emulation (`--wave64-emulate`, on by default there); cross-half wave ops in vertex, pixel and geometry shaders are still approximate | | SPIR-V validation (`spirv-val`) | ✅ **26,503 / 26,503 passed** in the LLVM 23.1.5 Linux rerun at `c432cdc` and in the full-corpus rerun at `43d4703`, after `dcd8ecf` fixed the SPIR-V ID-bound error ([Linux rerun](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida/issues/644#issuecomment-7072972586), [full-corpus rerun](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida/issues/881#issuecomment-7075507328)). On Windows at `43d0015`, all 26,503 translated but 26,501 passed validation; the two ID-bound failures were fixed by `dcd8ecf`. The intermediate `dedd75c` run also passed 26,501. | | Shader translator checked on a real GPU | ⚠️ The hand-written GPU tests (vertex fetch, texture sampling, exports, ALU ops, partial-register ops, barycentrics, wave-uniform branches, compute LDS/barriers/buffer stores, wave64 masks) have been run on more than 30 GPU and driver combinations, with results in [#166](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida/issues/166): NVIDIA Turing, Ampere, Ada and Blackwell (Windows and Linux); AMD GCN3, RDNA1, RDNA2, RDNA3 and RDNA4 (Windows driver and RADV); Intel Gen9 (ANV); Apple M1 (MoltenVK, no geometry or mesh stages); and Mesa llvmpipe. Wave64 tests need 64-wide subgroups (AMD) or `LEONIDA_W64_EMULATE=1`. These are small test shaders: the game's own shaders are checked by `spirv-val` and by driver pipeline creation (`vk_pipeline_check`), not by their output | | Models (OBJ with real names, UVs, material references) | ✅ Exported. A ten-archive scan at decoder pin `e293917` recovered **382,781 models** with zero readback decode failures. This includes **343,327** models from `levels.rpf`. A full OBJ export of that archive is pending. See [recount and export scope](docs/models.md#full-archive-re-count-at-e293917). | | Texture dictionaries and world texture pools (DDS) | ✅ Exported. Pool entries stored as BCPack are still skipped by the export; a clean-room decoder (`tools/bcpack.py`) rebuilds BC1, BC3, BC4, BC5, BC6H and BC7 (most BC6H/BC7 chunks need a local history table, which the repo does not ship), and is not wired into `rpf9dump` yet ([notes](docs/textures.md)) | | Models (OBJ with real names, UVs, material references) | ✅ Exported. Not all layouts are decoded yet | | Texture dictionaries and world texture pools (DDS) | ✅ Exported. `rpf9dump` decodes BCPack BC1, BC3, BC4 and BC5 chunks in strict mode and skips BC6H, BC7 and chunks that need unconfirmed history; the assets stage then completes what it can with a clean-room decoder (`tools/bcpack.py`, run by `tools/ttpf_assets.py`) that rebuilds BC1, BC3, BC4, BC5, BC6H and BC7, and marks the rest as limited in `manifest.json` (most BC6H/BC7 chunks and the unconfirmed-history ones need a local history table, which the repo does not ship) ([notes](docs/textures.md)) | | Audio banks (AWC: Opus, XMA2) | ✅ Exported whole. Opus repackaged **losslessly** as Ogg Opus; PCM (codec 0/2) as WAV; XMA2 decoded with ffmpeg. `--wav` adds 16-bit PCM WAV ([notes](docs/audio.md)) | | Music/radio config | ? Measured. **1,589** audio-config records with exact durations and AWC stream ids; station grouping and content-id lists; no per-track start offsets ([notes](docs/audio_config.md)) | | PE loader and import shims | ⚠️ Runs a stand-in executable end to end (`gta6rt --run`: CRT startup, statics, heap, files, threads, GDK imports through the shims, exit code back). Controllers through a GameInput shim on SDL3 (any controller SDL supports, rumble, DualSense trigger effects and lightbar; built when SDL3 is installed or with `-DLEONIDA_SDL3_FETCH=ON`, [notes](docs/gameinput.md)). `--trace-d3d12` logs every D3D12 call and its outcome for the first boot. Untested against the real executable | | Xbox D3D12 → Vulkan | ⚠️ In progress. A Vulkan-backed device behind the Xbox-ABI proxy creates queues, command lists, fences, descriptor heaps, committed and reserved resources, render-target and depth views (3D targets included), texture views and samplers (2D, cube and 3D views, the depth and stencil planes of depth-stencil textures, packed formats such as B5G6R5, B4G4R4A4 and R9G9B9E5; they go into the bindless set), and query heaps. Barriers, clears, uploads, copies (BC included), colour resolves, predication, CPU-side texture reads and writes, and occlusion, timestamp and pipeline-statistics queries run on Vulkan, checked on one GPU. No buffer views, root signatures, pipelines, draws, placed resources, 1D textures or swapchain yet ([plan](docs/d3d12_vulkan.md)) | | Ray tracing (BVH) | ⚠️ In progress. `BuildRaytracingAccelerationStructure` builds BLASes and TLASes on the GPU in the console's XDXR BVH4 layout (the default; `LEONIDA_RT_AS=khr` uses Vulkan's own acceleration structures instead), which the translated shaders walk themselves through `image_bvh_intersect_ray` (all four triangle node types, TRI0-TRI3, with the barycentric remap byte); the GPU builder writes TRI0 leaves. Updates refit instead of rebuilding, and clone, compaction and the compacted/current postbuild sizes work; checked against a CPU reference on synthetic scenes. The build descriptions are recovered from the package's `XboxBvhBuilder.dll` ([notes](docs/xdxr.md)). The game's `*_bvh4.rpf` packs are measured: offline-built, dehydrated BLASes that rehydrate through that DLL with their geometry from the drawables in `levels.rpf` (measured on 8 of the 10 sampled BLAS; [notes](docs/bvh.md)). Not done in the builder: TRI1 pairing, BOX16 nodes, serialization. Open: whether the game rehydrates the packs or rebuilds them ([#313](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida/issues/313)) | | Xbox D3D12 → Vulkan | ⚠️ In progress. A Vulkan-backed device behind the Xbox-ABI proxy creates queues, command lists and bundles, fences, descriptor heaps, committed, placed and reserved resources (1D, 2D, 3D and cube textures), render-target and depth views, texture views, buffer UAVs and samplers (they go into the bindless set), root signatures, graphics (vertex, pixel, geometry) and compute pipelines, pipeline libraries, command signatures and query heaps. Draws (MSAA included), dispatches and indirect dispatches, barriers, clears, uploads, copies (BC included), colour and depth resolves, predication, CPU-side texture reads and writes, and occlusion, timestamp and pipeline-statistics queries run on Vulkan, as do DXGI swapchains and `PresentX` planes. Tested by contributors on NVIDIA, AMD and Intel GPUs ([#166](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida/issues/166)). Not yet: mesh-shader draws, the draw state of indirect draws, stream output, and anything checked against the real executable ([plan](docs/d3d12_vulkan.md)) | | Ray tracing (BVH) | ⚠️ In progress. `BuildRaytracingAccelerationStructure` builds BLASes and TLASes on the GPU in the console's XDXR BVH4 layout, which the translated shaders walk themselves (`image_bvh_intersect_ray`, TRI0/TRI1 leaves); `LEONIDA_RT_AS=khr` uses Vulkan's own acceleration structures instead. The build descriptions are recovered from the package's `XboxBvhBuilder.dll` ([notes](docs/xdxr.md)). The game's `*_bvh4.rpf` packs are measured: offline-built, dehydrated BLASes that rehydrate through that DLL with their geometry from the drawables in `levels.rpf` (measured on 8 of the 10 sampled BLAS; [notes](docs/bvh.md)). Not done in the builder: TRI1 pairing, BOX16 nodes, serialization. Open: whether the game rehydrates the packs or rebuilds them, and the XDXR-vs-KHR default ([#313](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida/issues/313)) | The table above is written by hand. To measure it on your own checkout (unit and runtime tests, which rows of the translator contract were confirmed on a GPU, measured imports, your corpus counts and, with `--github`, CI and the `D3D-` items), run `python -I tools/progress_dashboard.py --out ` and open `progress.html` ([notes](docs/progress_dashboard.md)). ## Platforms Nothing is playable on any platform yet (see *Project status*). What runs where today: | Platform | Today | |---|---| | Windows | Everything: `make_game.py`, the tools, and the runtime (`gta6rt` and the D3D12 → Vulkan layer) with its tests. | | Linux | The translator, the asset tools and the Vulkan GPU test tools build and run natively (tested on RADV and NVIDIA). The runtime is Windows code: it cross-compiles with clang-cl and xwin, and its tests run under Wine or Proton (*The Windows runtime on Linux, under Wine or Proton* below). The game is meant to run the same way, under Wine or Proton with the D3D12 layer on native Vulkan (#217). | | macOS (Apple Silicon) | The Python tools and the Vulkan test tools run natively, on MoltenVK (Homebrew) or KosmicKrisp. The runtime is Windows code and runs as on Linux, under Wine: CrossOver, arm64 with FEX or x86-64 under Rosetta (#1706, #1707, #1924; #3119 fixes the last loader tests there). Known gaps: no geometry stage and no `VK_EXT_mesh_shader` (those tests are skipped), 32-wide subgroups (wave64 shaders run emulated), and MoltenVK's float handling (`PerVertexKHR`, NaN compares, -0, the cost of `NoContraction`); [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md) lists each (#2947). | | AMD RDNA1 (RX 5000) | A supported target: close to the console's RDNA2, and its 64-wide subgroups run the wave64 shaders natively. RX 5700 XT results pass the GPU test suite (#146); on RADV, pixel shaders without fragment barycentrics have a known difference (*Known problems* in [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md)) (#330). | GPU results from every platform are collected in #166; how to run the tests is in [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md). ## How to build The port isn't downloaded ready-made. It's built on your PC from your own copy. **The easy way:** 1. Install the prerequisites below. 2. Download this project **with its submodule**: `git clone --recursive https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida`. A "Download ZIP" from GitHub leaves out `third_party/rpf9-explorer`. The build fetches it if `git` is installed, and otherwise tells you what to do. 3. Double-click **`Build.bat`**. It finds your copy of the game by itself: it looks in Downloads, Desktop, Documents (also where Windows keeps them, such as in OneDrive), Games, your home folder and the top of every drive, two folders deep. It recognises the version from a few file sizes, without reading anything large. If you have more than one copy it asks which one, and if it finds none it asks you to paste the folder. Before starting it checks that everything below is installed and that there is enough free space, and it lists anything missing in one go. The result goes to `Documents\Leonida`. A stopped build continues where it left off. Your game folder is the one that holds `MicrosoftGame.Config` and the `.rpf` archives, as plain files. **Prerequisites:** - **Your own copy** of the Xbox Series package, version 1.0.2.1. - **Windows 10/11 x64**, with about **350 GB** free for work files. They can go on another drive with `--work`. - [Python 3.12+](https://www.python.org/downloads/) (tick "Add python.exe to PATH"). - [.NET 8 SDK](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/8.0). - [Vulkan SDK](https://vulkan.lunarg.com/), for `spirv-as` / `spirv-val`. - [LLVM 21+](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/releases) with the **AMDGPU target** for `llvm-mc`. The official Windows build has no AMDGPU target. On Windows, `scripts\build_llvm_mc.ps1` builds a native `llvm-mc.exe` with it (no WSL; needs git and the Visual Studio C++ tools below) and sets `LLVM_MC`; it takes about 20-40 minutes. A faster way, if you use [conda](https://docs.conda.io/): `conda install -c conda-forge llvm-tools` (its Windows build includes the AMDGPU target; [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md) used version 23.1.6), then set `LLVM_MC` to the full path of the `llvm-mc.exe` it installs (`where llvm-mc` shows it once the environment is active). Or install `llvm-21` in WSL and set `LLVM_MC` to the whole command, `LLVM_MC="wsl -d Ubuntu -e /usr/lib/llvm-21/bin/llvm-mc"` (see [docs/design.md](docs/design.md#disassembling-shaders)). On Linux, `llvm-mc` on PATH is enough. - Visual Studio 2022 with **Desktop development with C++** and the **Windows SDK 10.0.26100 or newer**, for the runtime stage (the runtime uses version 1.2 root signatures, which older SDKs don't declare). - [ffmpeg](https://ffmpeg.org/download.html) on PATH (optional: decodes the XMA2 streams, and required for `--wav`). **Low disk space:** the ~350 GB figure is for the full build. To *run* the port, `--stages check,shaders,runtime` needs about 30 GB; the `assets` stage (~300 GB) is only for the asset tools, and `--wav` adds several times the Ogg Opus size (the preflight prints this choice when the assets stage is what does not fit). `--work` and `--out` can sit on another drive. The runtime maps the package in place, so a read-only package drive needs `gta6rt --overlay `; `--overlay` is a `gta6rt` option, not a `make_game.py` one. Leave the `.s` files in `work/shaders/dxbc/disasm` in place: deleting them, along with the translated `work/shaders/spirv/index.json`, can leave the shaders stage looking finished with zero shaders. A `disasm` folder that is a symlink is refused when the stage has to clear it. **From a terminal**, with the same behaviour and more control: ```powershell python -I make_game.py --find # list the copies found on this PC python -I make_game.py --pick # choose the game folder in a folder dialog python -I make_game.py --check # check your copy, build nothing python -I make_game.py --check --full-check # also compare SHA-256 of every file (slow) python -I make_game.py --game "D:\path\to\your\package" --out "D:\Games\Leonida" --work "E:\leonida-work" python -I make_game.py --stages shaders,assets # only some stages python -I make_game.py --game "D:\path\to\your\package" --wav # also decode Opus to PCM WAV (large) python -I make_game.py --wave64-emulate off # auto (default), on or off; see below ``` `--wave64-emulate` decides whether wave64 compute and mesh shaders are translated to be exact on any subgroup size (see "Wave64 emulation" in [docs/design.md](docs/design.md)). NVIDIA and Intel GPUs have 32-wide subgroups and need it. The default, `auto`, asks `vulkaninfo` (part of the Vulkan SDK) and turns emulation on if any GPU lacks 64-wide subgroups or its subgroup size is unknown. It also checks whether the runtime's GPU can run compute and mesh shaders 64-wide. With `--mesh-compute`, only compute subgroup support is needed. On AMD's Windows driver, `auto` uses native wave64 on RDNA1 and RDNA2 when the runtime's GPU supports it, even if another GPU is 32-wide or `vulkaninfo` is unavailable. That driver can crash on emulated LDS code (#857). For RDNA1 cards without mesh support, the decision uses the compute stage, which can run wave64 without native mesh support. The mode is saved next to the translated shaders, and changing it translates them again. `auto` can normally reuse previously emulated shaders. The AMD Windows workaround rebuilds those shaders in native mode. Use `--wave64-emulate on` to force emulation or `--wave64-emulate off` to force native wave64. Four fallback flags are forwarded to the translator the same way, saved next to the translated shaders, and changing them translates them again: `--no-float-controls` (drop `SignedZeroInfNanPreserve`, for devices whose pipeline check skips a shader without `shaderSignedZeroInfNanPreserveFloat32`; needs PR #664's translator flag), `--bary-fallback` (read raw barycentrics from an interpolated input, for devices without `VK_KHR_fragment_shader_barycentric`), `--texel-offset-fallback` (fold `image_sample*_o` offsets into the coordinate, for devices without `VK_KHR_maintenance8`) and `--mesh-compute` (mesh shaders as compute, for devices without `VK_EXT_mesh_shader`). Each is documented in [docs/design.md](docs/design.md). The build records which llvm-mc command and version produced the disassembly. Changing either, or reusing a work folder that predates this record, reruns disassembly and translation while keeping the extracted shader inputs. The build records which translator sources produced the shaders. A change to those files reruns translation using the saved disassembly. Older work folders need one translation after upgrading to record this information. The build also records which decoder (the `third_party/rpf9-explorer` commit and the `tools/rpf9dump` sources) exported each archive's models and textures. When it changes, the assets stage removes that export and makes it again. Older work folders have no record, so their models and textures are exported once more after upgrading. Stages run in order: `check`, `shaders`, `assets`, `runtime`, `pipelines` (creates every translated shader on your GPU driver and checks that it compiles, reports any it has to skip, and saves a pipeline cache to `pipeline_cache.bin` in `--out`; the runtime doesn't load that cache yet, so it doesn't speed up the first boot). The shader translation is the longest step: it runs on `--jobs` processes (half the CPU threads by default). `--wav` is off by default because 16-bit PCM WAV is several times larger than Ogg Opus. It decodes the repackaged Ogg Opus streams to `work\assets\audio\wav` after the audio bank step; existing WAV files are skipped when a build resumes. ### Vulkan diagnostics on Linux With CMake 3.24+, a C++20 compiler, and Vulkan development headers and loader installed: ```sh cmake -S runtime -B runtime/build/linux cmake --build runtime/build/linux --parallel ./runtime/build/linux/vk_pipeline_check /path/to/spirv ``` Pass the directory containing `index.json` and the translated SPIR-V files to `vk_pipeline_check`. `make_game.py` runs on Linux too. The `pipelines` stage uses the `vk_pipeline_check` built above (`runtime/build/linux`, or `runtime/build`), and builds it there itself before any other work if it is missing. ### Running the loader on Linux The loader is a Windows program and runs under Wine or Proton; CI runs its tests under Wine on every push to `main` that changes `runtime/`, and on demand from the Actions tab (the `wine` job of the Runtime workflow). On Linux the `runtime` stage cross-builds it into `runtime/build/windows` with clang-cl and lld-link (LLVM 19+, but not 22.1.7 or 22.1.8, see [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md#known-problems); plain names, or all five LLVM tools with one version suffix such as `clang-cl-21`) against the MSVC CRT and Windows SDK that [xwin](https://github.com/Jake-Shadle/xwin) lays out, in `XWIN_DIR` or `~/.local/share/xwin-sdk` ([docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md#the-windows-runtime-on-linux-under-wine-or-proton) has the one-time `xwin` command). Without them the stage is left out of the default stages, and asking for it lists what is missing before any work starts. A Windows build made elsewhere works too, such as the `runtime-windows` artifact of that workflow's `windows` job, unzipped: ```sh python3 -I make_game.py --runtime-build ~/Downloads/runtime-windows ``` Either way it copies `gta6rt.exe` and `gta6rt_tls_host.dll` into `--out` and writes `gta6rt.sh` next to them, which starts `gta6rt.exe` with `wine`, or with the Wine named by `WINE` (for Proton, its `files/bin/wine`). The same option skips the build on Windows. ## How it works | Piece | What it does | Where | |---|---|---| | Version check | Every package file's name, size and SHA-256 for each supported version | `game/`, `make_game.py` | | Shader pipeline | Carves DXBC containers from `shaders.rpf` without its encrypted table of contents. Unpacks the `XBCH` → `FSSM` native RDNA2 program, disassembles it with LLVM (`gfx1013`) and translates it to SPIR-V | `tools/shader_carve.py`, `fssm_unpack.py`, `shader_disasm.py`, `rdna2spirv.py` | | Asset export | Finds validated resources inside RPF9 archives and the loose `.ttpf` texture pools | `tools/rpf9dump` (on rpf9-explorer's Core) | | Runtime | Maps the PE image, resolves imports to shims (GDK, XMem, `d3d12_xs`) | `runtime/` | | Research tools | PE/RTTI inspection, raw carving, texture tiling probes, GPU test harnesses | `tools/`, `runtime/test/` | | Progress dashboard | One offline page of what passes, what changed since it last passed and what blocks next, built from test results and the docs' own tables; nothing is written inside the repo | `tools/progress_dashboard.py` | The translator's runtime contract (user SGPRs, push constants, memory model, bindless images, vertex fetch, system values) and all the format notes are in [docs/design.md](docs/design.md); the format, asset, runtime and validation notes are indexed in [docs/README.md](docs/README.md). The Xbox D3D12 plan is in [docs/d3d12_vulkan.md](docs/d3d12_vulkan.md). Audio bank formats and the export tools are in [docs/audio.md](docs/audio.md); [docs/related_projects.md](docs/related_projects.md) records the prior art we may read and the licence limits on it. ## Want to help? The biggest open pieces: - **Shader translator on hardware**: compute, mesh and geometry now translate (see the translator contract in [docs/design.md](docs/design.md)); still open are the vertex-shader input layout (`v0` = `VertexIndex` is unverified if the console runs VS as NGG) and wave64 cross-half code in VS/PS/GS on 32-wide subgroups. - **Xbox D3D12 → Vulkan**: the `d3d12_xs` command list and descriptor heap model. - **Model recovery**: investigate the 71 unrecovered fragment candidates in [`levels.rpf`](docs/models.md#full-archive-re-count-at-e293917). See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). Never attach game files, extracted assets or generated shaders to issues or pull requests. ## Credits - [rpf9-explorer](https://github.com/breadbbbb/rpf9-explorer) by breadbbbb: the RPF9 model, texture-pool and AWC decoders used by `tools/rpf9dump` (git submodule). - [Mesa](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa) (MIT): GFX10 resource-descriptor layout (`tools/gfx10_formats.json`), and the ACO/RADV rules used as reference for 16-bit results and shader system registers. - [libHttpClient](https://github.com/microsoft/libHttpClient) (MIT) by Microsoft: the XTaskQueue/XAsync implementation in `third_party/xtaskqueue`, used by the offline `xgameruntime` shim. - [LLVM](https://llvm.org/): AMDGPU disassembler. - Logo: ["Grand Theft Auto VI" icon by SlyDevil](https://www.steamgriddb.com/icon/122618) on SteamGridDB. - [SPIRV-Tools](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/SPIRV-Tools): assembly and validation. ﻿# mcp-for-blender-pro

### Your Blender scene. Your AI models. One creative workspace.


**An AI assistant for Blender that can inspect your scene, build objects, edit materials, find assets and carry out multi-step workflows—with a visual chat workspace and a built-in Model Context Protocol (MCP) server.**


![Blender 4.2+](https://img.shields.io/badge/Blender-4.2%2B-E87D0D?logo=blender&logoColor=white)
![Release 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/release-1.0.0-98D85B)
![Windows x64](https://img.shields.io/badge/download-Windows_x64-357EC7)
![MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)


[Download](https://github.com/bookwjitchieni1986/blender-ai-mcp-addon/releases/latest) · [Getting started](docs/QUICKSTART.md) · [Connections and agents](docs/CONNECTIONS.md)


![AI chat workspace with a live Blender scene preview](docs/images/studio.png)


## Turn a creative brief into scene operations


Start with an idea. Ask the assistant to inspect your scene, create a product-display layout, arrange objects, assign materials or prepare an export. Follow its actions in the conversation and inspect the result in the viewport preview. Keep working in Blender throughout the process.


**mcp-for-blender-pro brings conversation, scene tools, model choice and agent workflows together.** It is designed for artists who want faster iteration, technical artists who automate repetitive work, and developers connecting AI tools to Blender.


## Why choose mcp-for-blender-pro?


| Capability | What it gives you |
|---|---|
| **Blender-aware assistance** | Scene and object inspection gives the assistant context before it acts. |
| **A visual Studio workspace** | Chat, scene objects, viewport snapshots, approvals and a task board in a companion window. |
| **Your choice of AI** | Connect supported cloud providers, local Ollama models or compatible custom endpoints. |
| **Saved connections** | Keep work and personal connections separate, including multiple keys for the same provider. |
| **One assistant or a team** | Use a single model for quick changes, or managers, workers and reviewers for structured tasks. |
| **Built-in MCP server** | Connect OpenCode and other clients supporting authenticated Streamable HTTP MCP. |
| **21 scene tools** | Create, inspect, edit, capture, search assets, consult Blender APIs and export scenes. |
| **Multilingual menus** | Choose English, German, French, Spanish or Chinese for the main interface. |


## From a quick edit to an agent team


Use **Single assistant** for direct, conversational work. For larger tasks, configure a **Team chain** with individual responsibilities, instructions and models.


- **Manager:** breaks the request into assignments and acceptance criteria.
- **Workers:** perform the assigned scene operations.
- **Reviewers:** inspect results and approve work or return specific findings.


Tasks run sequentially so scene edits stay ordered. A blocked task gets one correction attempt; a second failed review stops the workflow. The task board exposes assignments, attempts and review findings as work progresses.


![Agent roles and model configuration](docs/images/studio-team.png)


## Connect the models that fit your work


Supported connections include **OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, OpenRouter, OpenCode Zen, Ollama and custom APIs**. Load the available model catalog and select a model directly in Blender or Studio.


Custom endpoints support OpenAI Chat Completions, Anthropic Messages and Ollama protocols. Choose models with tool-calling support; image-capable models can also interpret viewport screenshots. OpenCode-only free models are available through the OpenCode client.


![Provider, saved connection and model selection](docs/images/studio-settings.png)


## Install and create


1. Download **`mcp-for-blender-pro.zip`** from [Releases](../../releases/latest).
2. In Blender, open **Edit → Preferences → Get Extensions → menu → Install from Disk**.
3. Select the ZIP, enable **mcp-for-blender-pro**, then open **3D Viewport → N → MCP Pro**.
4. Choose a provider, add your connection details and select a model.
5. Send a message in Blender or click **Open Studio Window**.


The release bundle targets **Windows x64 with Blender 4.2 or later**. Keep Blender open while using Studio or an external client.


### Try these prompts


> Inspect this scene and explain its object structure before making any changes.


> Create a simple product-display scene with a pedestal, a camera and three lights. Give the pedestal a matte blue material.


> Duplicate the selected object into a neatly spaced row of five and show the viewport.


> Find an appropriate Poly Haven asset for this scene and ask before importing it.


## Blender automation through MCP


Launch **OpenCode Portable** from the sidebar to work through OpenCode with the Blender connection configured for you. OpenCode manages its own provider sign-in and model selection. Other compatible MCP clients can connect to the authenticated local endpoint described in the [connection guide](docs/CONNECTIONS.md).

## Stay in control of your scene


Built-in chat supports operation approvals, cancellation after the current step and named undo steps for mutations. Python tool validation helps catch disallowed operations; it is not a security sandbox. External MCP clients manage their own approval policies.


Connection credentials are stored in your user settings. Chat history lasts for the current session. Studio runs locally and authenticates requests to Blender.

items.title: EL4CTEO/fast-anything
items.description: Don't rewrite it in Rust. Rewrite the 5% that's slow: profile Python, Node or Ruby apps, port the hot functions with your coding agent, prove they behave the same.
items.readme:
Don't rewrite it in Rust. Rewrite the 5% that's slow.

Rewriting a whole app in Rust costs months, minute-long compiles and gigabytes of `target/`. Most of the runtime sits in a few functions anyway. **fast-anything** finds those functions, has your coding agent port *only them* to Rust, proves the port gives the same results on real recorded calls, and swaps it in. One command, fully reversible.

## Install ```sh npm i -g @el4cteo/fast-anything # or: cargo install fast-anything ``` Ports are compiled with your Rust toolchain ([rustup](https://rustup.rs)). ## Use ```sh fast-anything go --agent claude -- python app.py # or: -- node app.ts / bun app.ts / deno run -A app.ts / ruby app.rb / java App.java / mvn exec:java / gradle run / go run . / php app.php / clang -O2 main.c / Rscript app.R ``` Or step by step: | command | what it does | |---|---| | `scan -- ` | profiles the app, ranks functions by time × how portable they are | | `port [id]` | records up to 500 real calls, creates a one-function Rust crate + `TASK.md` | | `verify` | release-builds the port and replays every recorded call | | `enable` / `disable` | swaps the Rust in or out (one marked block, removed byte for byte) | | `bench` | times the whole app, original vs Rust, interleaved runs | | `report` | markdown + SVG card for your PR | | `doctor` | checks Rust, your runtimes and your agents | `--agent` takes `claude`, `codex`, or any command that reads a prompt on stdin. Without it, hand `TASK.md` to whatever you use. ## Proof, not vibes

That port looked right but compared bytes instead of characters. 148 of 500 real calls caught it. On top of the recorded calls, fast-anything derives extra cases and lets the original answer them: edge cases (NaN, ±infinity, -0.0, zero and ±1, non-ASCII text, empty and up to 16× bigger inputs) and shrunk inputs (tiny and random slices). Nothing is enabled until every case matches: same values (floats within 1e-9), errors where the original errors. A port that is right but slower per call than the original (calling into Rust costs more than the work saved) isn't enabled either. `FAST_ANYTHING_DISABLE=1` runs the original any time. ## Results Real runs on an i5-10500, Windows 11 (C and C++: a 4-core GitHub Actions Linux runner). Reproduce them from [`examples/`](examples). | app | before | after | |---|---|---| | Python fuzzy dedupe (700 names) | 4.91s | **42ms, 116×** | | TypeScript fuzzy dedupe (2,000 names) | 3.11s | **155ms, 20×** | | PHP fuzzy dedupe (600 names) | 2.94s | **53ms, 55×** | | Go fuzzy dedupe (3,000 names) | 3.02s | **144ms, 21×** | | Ruby fuzzy dedupe (400 names) | 3.13s | **228ms, 14×** | | C# fuzzy dedupe (4,000 names) | 4.03s | **312ms, 13×** | | Java fuzzy dedupe (4,000 names) | 3.50s | **1.18s, 3×** (11× on the function; the rest is JVM startup) | | C mandelbrot (8 zoom levels) | 431ms | **127ms, 3.4×** | | C++ fuzzy dedupe (6,000 names) | 3.02s | **1.09s, 2.7×** | fast-anything ports the outermost loop it can, not the tiny function called inside it, so the app crosses into Rust once instead of millions of times. Porting only the inner `levenshtein` gave 35× and 1.9×. ## Why not rewrite it all? - **Compile time**: each port is a one-function crate. Seconds, not minutes. - **Cache**: every port shares one `.fast/target`. Delete it whenever you like. - **Risk**: your code stays as it is. Rust is opt-in per function, checked against real behavior. ## Agents - **Claude Code plugin**: `/plugin marketplace add EL4CTEO/fast-anything`, then `/plugin install fast-anything@fast-anything` and `/fast-anything:fast python app.py` - **MCP server** (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor…), built into the binary: `claude mcp add fast-anything -- fast-anything mcp`. 8 tools: `fast_scan`, `fast_port`, `fast_verify`, `fast_enable`, `fast_disable`, `fast_bench`, `fast_report`, `fast_status`. - **Skill**: [`skills/fast-anything`](skills/fast-anything/SKILL.md) teaches any agent the loop. ## Languages | language | binding | status | |---|---|---| | Python 3.10+ | PyO3 | ✅ | | JavaScript / TypeScript (Node 22+, Bun, Deno 2+: `bun app.ts`, `deno run -A app.ts`) | napi-rs | ✅ | | Ruby 3.3+ | C ABI + JSON, through Ruby's built-in Fiddle | ✅ | | Java 22+ (`java App.java`, Maven, Gradle) | the same C bridge, through the FFM API | ✅ | | Kotlin/JVM (Gradle, `src/main/kotlin`, JDK 22+) | the Java bridge; top-level functions, `object` and companion members, extension functions | ✅ | | Go 1.22+ (`go run .`) | the same C bridge, through the Windows loader or dlopen (cgo) | ✅ | | PHP 8.1+ (`php app.php`) | the same C bridge, through PHP's FFI extension (`extension=ffi`) | ✅ | | C and C++ (gcc, clang or Intel oneAPI icx/icpx: `clang -O2 main.c lib.c`) | the same C bridge, through LoadLibrary or dlopen | ✅ | | C# / .NET 8+ (`dotnet run -c Release`) | the same C bridge, through NativeLibrary; profiled with EventPipe, nothing to install | ✅ | | R 4.0+ (`Rscript app.R`) | the same C bridge, through base R's `.C()`; profiled with Rprof, no packages or R headers needed | ✅ | It ports top-level, deterministic functions that take plain data (numbers, strings, lists, dicts, typed arrays…), including ones in your entry script when its main code sits under `if __name__ == "__main__":` (or `if __FILE__ == $0`, or `if (import.meta.main)` / `if (require.main === module)`). In Python that means module-level functions and `@staticmethod`s (dataclasses, NamedTuples and numeric NumPy arrays count as plain data), in Java, C# and PHP static methods (and PHP functions), in Go plain functions, in C and C++ free functions and static methods. `scan` says why anything else can't move yet. With Intel oneAPI on Windows, run fast-anything from a shell where `setvars.bat` ran (it sets up the linker). SYCL kernels run on the device and aren't ported; with `-fsycl`, only host functions are profiled and ported. Ruby, Java, Go, PHP, C, C++, C# and R need no headers, bindings or extra tools: the port is a plain Rust library with one C entry point taking and returning JSON, and fast-anything replays the recorded calls against it directly. Any language that can call C can use that bridge. ## License MIT

items.description: Paste a link, get captioned 9:16 clips in ~2 min. Free, local, open-source clipping engine (audio-first, YouTube captions, local LLM).
items.readme:
# NeonClipping

**Paste a link. Get captioned 9:16 clips in about two minutes. Free, local, open-source.**

NeonClipping turns long YouTube / Twitch / Kick videos (or your own MP4) into vertical, captioned clips with a title and hook for each. Everything runs on your machine: no account, no subscription, no upload.

[![Star on GitHub](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/iamajmeena/neonclipping?style=for-the-badge&logo=github&label=Star%20on%20GitHub)](https://github.com/iamajmeena/neonclipping) [![Instagram](https://img.shields.io/badge/Follow-%40iamajmeena-E4405F?style=for-the-badge&logo=instagram&logoColor=white)](https://www.instagram.com/iamajmeena/)

🌐 **Website with one-click Windows setup:** <https://iamajmeena.github.io/neonclipping/>

**Made by [Ajay K Meena](https://www.instagram.com/iamajmeena/)** (Director, DOP, colorist, DaVinci Resolve educator, Jaipur). If NeonClipping saves you time, please ⭐ star the repo and follow [@iamajmeena](https://www.instagram.com/iamajmeena/) on Instagram.

**Clip an 85-minute stream in 97 seconds, 100% locally, with zero API cost.** (measured, see [How it finds good moments](#how-it-finds-good-moments))

### NeonClipping compared with other clippers

| | **NeonClipping** | OpusClip (cloud) | Docker-based self-hosted clippers (SupoClip, OpenShorts, Reelsaw) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Where it runs | Your PC, nothing uploaded | Their servers | Your machine or server |
| Cost | Free, no account, no credits | Subscription / credits | Free (some need an LLM API key or Docker setup) |
| Install | One `.bat` on Windows, `install.sh` on Mac/Linux, no Docker | None (web) | Docker |
| YouTube + Twitch + Kick links | Yes | Yes | Mostly YouTube |
| Very long streams | Audio-first (79 MB for 85 min); 24 h video: pick the part, never downloads all | Upload limits apply | Often limited by length or disk |
| Gaming layouts (facecam + gameplay) | 11 layouts, automatic facecam finder | Limited | Varies |
| Live stream clipping | Yes, chat-spike based, phone remote | No | Rarely |
| Download quality | 1080p default, 4K option beside Get preview | n/a | Varies |
| Captions | 5 styles, 52 languages, Hinglish, on/off, quiet-part aware | Templates | Varies |

![demo](docs/demo.gif)

![UI](docs/neonclipping-ui.jpg)

📘 **Guides (Hindi + English, PDF):** [docs/NeonClipping-Guide-EN-HI.pdf](docs/NeonClipping-Guide-EN-HI.pdf)  
🤖 **Let an AI agent install it for you:** copy [docs/NEONCLIPPING-AGENT-SETUP-PROMPT.txt](docs/NEONCLIPPING-AGENT-SETUP-PROMPT.txt) into Claude Code, Codex CLI or Cursor.

## How it finds good moments

Two modes, one button.

**⚡ Fast mode (default, videos over 10 min)** copies the trick that makes the fastest clippers fast: never look at the whole video.

1. Download **audio only** (79 MB for an 85-minute video, about 10 s).
2. Take the transcript for free from YouTube's own captions (word-timed). No speech model needed. For other sources a local Whisper model is used as the fallback.
3. Score the whole audio track for *sudden loudness jumps* (vs a 2-minute local baseline), *raised voices* (2–4 kHz energy) and quiet-to-loud transitions.
4. Take the best moments, read each one's transcript with a local LLM (Ollama) and let it score the moment, write a title and a hook. Snap the start and end to sentence boundaries inside your Min/Max length.
5. Download **only the chosen sections** of the video (not the whole file), trim exactly by matching their sound to the audio track, and render 1080x1920 clips with burned-in captions.

**🔬 Deep mode** downloads the whole video, adds optical-flow motion (OpenCV Farneback: fast objects, impacts, camera whips) and cut density to the audio signals, shortlists 4× more candidates and gives the LLM 15 seconds of context before and after each one.

Measured on one machine (RTX 2060, 16 threads), Fast mode, 3 clips each:

| Source | Time |
|---|---|
| 85-minute YouTube stream (YouTube captions) | **97 s** |
| 3-hour Twitch VOD (no captions, local speech model) | **136 s** |
| 90-second YouTube trailer | 21 s |
| 90-second local MP4 | 14 s |

Your numbers depend on network and CPU.

## How it decides what is a good moment

Every candidate moment is scored from several signals, then the best ones are kept:

| Signal | What it looks for |
|---|---|
| Loudness jump | A sudden boom or shout compared with the last two minutes |
| Raised voice | Energy in the 2–4 kHz band (screaming, yelling) |
| What is said | "oh my god", "oh shit", "run", "police", "bhaago", "arre yaar" and similar (English, Hinglish, Hindi) |
| On-screen action | Fast motion (optical flow), explosion-like flashes, red/blue light flicker, scene cuts |
| AI score | A small local LLM reads the transcript: emotion, punchline, payoff |

**It learns from you.** Generated moments have five-star controls in results and My clips. Ratings stay on your computer (`data/feedback.jsonl`). After at least eight **different moments**, with a useful mix of stronger/weaker ratings and different measurements, the local ranking weights can adapt. Repeated clicks update that moment's latest rating; re-edited versions keep one training identity. The full rating history stays intact. This fits a small preference ranker, not the foundation model. Nothing is uploaded.

## Features

- One-click **Make clips**, live progress, clips appear one by one with preview and MP4 download.
- **Min / Max clip length** (e.g. 30–80 s). Clips end on a sentence.
- **Facecam position presets** (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right, bottom-centre, none) for the usual streamer layouts, remembered between sessions. Or draw the face and gameplay boxes yourself in the editor.
- **11 native layouts:** camera above/below gameplay, blurred fill, full-screen crop, gameplay only, four corner overlays, circle facecam and side-by-side. Independent face/game selection and a face-size slider. Preview-only platform safe zones.
- Caption styles: GTA Neon, Impact, Clean, Hormozi and MrBeast. Word-timed, editable words, SRT export.
- **Opening headings:** eight seconds by default, adjustable from 2–60 seconds, with black backing for bright gameplay and facecam layouts. Use **Improve opening heading** to write a grounded curiosity question from the selected transcript. Existing clips can apply the new look without downloading or finding moments again.
- **Moment mix:** Balanced combines activity and transcript-led proposals; Action favours energy; Dialogue favours story, humour and insights. Final selection reduces overlapping and repetitive moments. Balanced/Dialogue prefer an already-installed Gemma 4 local judge; other local models remain a fallback. This changes curation rules and prompts, not foundation-model weights.
- **Custom captions:** installed font family, size, text/active/outline colours, words per caption and local saved profiles. Import SRT/ASS/WebVTT or paste subtitle text, adjust word timings, split/merge and shift captions. Within-cue word timings from imported files are estimated. Download WebVTT alongside SRT.
- **Transcript explorer:** explicitly generate or import a full-source transcript, search phrases across cues, browse pages, and click the first/last word to export that passage. Cached transcripts are reused by Make clips and invalidated when the source changes.
- **Trim a saved clip:** in *Edit saved clips*, change Start / End and press *Only this clip*; the clip is cut again from the saved video and the subtitles move with the cut (3 to 180 s, within the saved video).
- **52 caption languages** in the Language menu, see Honest limits for caveats.
- **Optional visual review:** an already-installed compatible Gemma4 image model describes three actual scene frames. Review them in the editor or enable visual review for automatic candidate refinement. It is off by default and can add CPU inference time. Sampled image descriptions can be uncertain and do not verify a complete game event. Saved evidence is reused during re-editing.
- **Hinglish captions**: Hindi speech is written in English letters ("kya haal hai bhai") by default. Pick Hinglish / हिंदी / English explicitly if you like. Fast uses available source captions; Best Hindi explicitly uses local large-v3 recognition and can be slower on small GPUs. Missing source captions require local recognition.
- **Make clips uses your own setup**: facecam preset or the boxes you draw in step 03.
- Optical-flow motion + audio highlight ranking, frame-accurate NVENC export (falls back to x264).
- Nothing leaves your computer. The server binds to `127.0.0.1` only.

## Change clips after generating them

![Saved clip editor with eleven layouts](docs/saved-clip-editor.jpg)

Open **My clips → Edit clip**. The saved editor includes all **11 speaker position/shape layouts**, a speaker-size slider, editable subtitle words, caption style and caption height.

- **Apply to this clip** updates the opened clip.
- **Apply to this video's clips** updates the currently saved clips associated with the same source URL. Each keeps its own timestamps, transcript, title and hook. New clips still being generated are not included in that snapshot.
- Source download, highlight discovery and speech recognition are **not repeated**. Burned-in captions and framing require encoding a new final MP4.
- Original source files must remain in `data/`. Previous MP4s are kept; the library displays the latest versions. Old exports missing saved word timings can recover captions from their SRT, with approximate per-word timing.
- This edits the selected moments; changing the clip's start/end or spoken language requires a separate trim/transcription workflow.

Validation on one 796.9-second source: all 11 layouts and five caption styles exported with audio and decoded successfully. A seven-clip layout/style update took 119.58 seconds while reusing each clip's exact source, range and word list. These are local checks, not guaranteed runtimes or a caption-quality benchmark.

Run the portable regression tests with `python -m unittest discover -s tests -v`.

## Install

**Easiest (Windows):** download [`NeonClipping-Setup.bat`](https://github.com/iamajmeena/neonclipping/releases/latest/download/NeonClipping-Setup.bat) from the [website](https://iamajmeena.github.io/neonclipping/) or the Releases page and double-click it. It checks your PC, installs Python and FFmpeg if missing, installs NeonClipping into `%LOCALAPPDATA%\NeonClipping`, creates a Desktop shortcut and opens the app. Mac/Linux: `install.sh` (new, not yet tested on a real Mac). Or follow the steps below.

Requirements: Python 3.10 to 3.13 (the newest Python often has no wheels for the speech/vision packages yet; the Mac/Linux installer picks a supported one for you), FFmpeg on PATH. Optional but recommended: [Ollama](https://ollama.com) with `ollama pull llama3.2:3b` for AI titles, hooks and scores (without it clips are picked by the audio/motion score), and an NVIDIA GPU for NVENC and faster-whisper.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/iamajmeena/neonclipping
cd neonclipping
# Windows
./run.ps1
# Linux / macOS
./run.sh
```

Open <http://127.0.0.1:8770>, paste a link, press **⚡ Make clips**.

Optional GPU speech model support (only used when a video has no YouTube captions):

```bash
.venv/bin/pip install nvidia-cublas-cu12 "nvidia-cudnn-cu12==9.*"
```

Set `NEONCLIPPING_CPU=1` to force CPU. Set `NEONCLIPPING_PORT=9000` to use another port.

**Mac / Linux / no NVIDIA GPU:** the video encoder is chosen by what works on your computer: NVIDIA NVENC, then Apple VideoToolbox, then the CPU encoder (x264). Force one with `NEONCLIPPING_ENCODER=nvenc|videotoolbox|x264`. The speech model skips the GPU attempt when no CUDA GPU exists and runs on the CPU. `install.sh` and the unit tests run automatically on macOS, Ubuntu and Windows machines for every change (see the *Actions* tab); the maintainer has not yet tried the Mac installer on his own Mac, so tell us if it misbehaves (Report a problem).

**Settings (environment variables):** `NEONCLIPPING_LIVE_AUTO_HOURS` (default 3) and `NEONCLIPPING_MIN_FREE_GB` (default 8) control the unattended creator-watch live sessions; a manual Live clipping session has no time cap and no disk guard.

## How it is built

| File | Job |
|---|---|
| `app.py` | FastAPI server, `/make` pipeline, export, library |
| `smart.py` | Moment scoring: transcript + local LLM, sentence snapping |
| `highlights.py` | Audio-jump / shout / optical-flow / cut ranking, parallel decode |
| `captions_yt.py` | YouTube word-timed captions (json3) parser |
| `captions.py` | Local Whisper (GPU first, CPU fallback), ASS/SRT styles |
| `translit.py` | Devanagari → Hinglish (word by word, keeps timings) |
| `standalone.py`, `previews.py` | Link import, early preview frames |

## Live clipping (while the stream is on)

Paste a Twitch channel link or a YouTube Live link into the **Live clipping** panel and press Start. NeonClipping records the stream (Streamlink), reads chat anonymously, counts messages in 10 s buckets and cuts a clip around every chat spike (chat velocity more than 2.5 sigma and 2.5x the 5-minute baseline). The clip starts about 24 s *before* the spike, because chat reacts after the moment. It then gets captions, a hook and title, your layout and facecam boxes, and a viral score like any other clip. **Clip the last 30 s now** cuts on demand, **Stop** ends the session. It only works while the stream is live; for finished videos use Make clips.

There is also a command-line version in `live/live_clip.py`.

## Creators (clip a streamer automatically)

Add a Twitch name or a Twitch / YouTube channel link in the **Creators** panel. NeonClipping checks every minute; when that creator goes live it records the stream and clips the chat spikes, using the layout, facecam boxes and caption style you had selected when you added them (“Use my current layout” updates it). Clips appear under the creator and in My clips.

- One stream at a time (recording and rendering are heavy); other creators wait their turn.
- NeonClipping must stay open. Unattended recordings stop after 3 hours (a new one starts if the creator is still live), stop when less than 8 GB of disk is free, and the big recording file is deleted after the last clip is cut.
- Pressing **Stop** pauses that creator for 30 minutes; switching Auto off and on resumes at once.
- Tested on Twitch (recording, chat spikes, clip, feed). YouTube channels are detected through yt-dlp; an auto-clipped YouTube stream was not run end to end.

## Tests

`tests/` holds an end-to-end suite that runs against the live server: page and API validation, every layout and caption style rendered and measured, editing one / all clips of a video, Make clips on real YouTube / Twitch / local sources in every mode and language, live clipping on a real stream, the creator list, star ratings, the installer and the website. Unit tests cover the chat-spike rule, caption grouping and re-editing. The last full run is in [`tests/REPORT.md`](tests/REPORT.md): 187 checks, all passing, plus the 12 problems the run found and fixed.

```
python -m unittest tests.test_captions tests.test_live tests.test_reedit
python tests/e2e.py static export edit creators feedback   # server must be running
python tests/e2e_make.py          # real downloads + transcription (about 25 min)
python tests/e2e_live.py          # needs a Twitch channel that is live
python tests/e2e_site.py          # website, links, release assets
python tests/make_report.py       # rebuild tests/REPORT.md
```

## Live clipping controls and the phone remote

Inspired by a mobile live-clipper shown in a creator's reel (that app is unreleased, so nothing of it could be studied; only what the video shows was used).

- **Chat hype meter** while a stream is live: 0-100%, from the comments of the last ~30 s against the stream's own usual speed (peak = 4x usual; the first seconds use an absolute scale), with the label *quiet / building momentum / hot / peak viral hype*.
- **Clip length presets** 10 s / 20 s / 30 s / Auto: the clip starts a few seconds before the chat peak; "Clip now" cuts the same length from the live recording.
- **Hook text** for live clips from the AI, the **stream title** (emoji removed) or your own text; **captions switch** (off = faster clips).
- Live clips now also get the style options (template, logo, credit, outro, music, caption animation).
- **Phone remote:** start NeonClipping with the *NeonClipping (phone access)* shortcut (`Start-NeonClipping-Phone.bat`, or set `NEONCLIPPING_LAN=1`). Under Live clipping it shows a Wi-Fi address and a 6-digit PIN. On a phone on the same Wi-Fi open that address (`/m`), enter the PIN, paste a YouTube Live or Twitch link, pick a length, watch the hype meter, press **Clip now**, and play / save / share the clips. On Android Chrome use "Add to Home screen" to get an app icon. The PC does all the work; the phone is only a remote.
- **Safety:** phone access is off unless you start it that way (the server then listens on 127.0.0.1 only). Everything that is not the PC needs the PIN (after 5 wrong tries an address is locked for 10 minutes; "New PIN" logs every phone out). Even with the PIN a phone can only use the live, library, make, clips, feedback and creators routes: uploads, file tools, the queue and the PIN itself stay PC-only. Windows will ask once whether to allow NeonClipping on private networks: choose Allow for home Wi-Fi only.
- Not included: a native Android app (the phone page is a web page that works like one), live clipping that runs on the phone itself.

## Captions: YouTube's own, always

For YouTube links every clip uses YouTube's own word-timed captions, in every language. Hindi comes as Devanagari and is turned into Hinglish (nukta letters included: kapde, padega, thoda); repeated-word loops are trimmed. It is faster than a local speech model and, on game audio, clearly more accurate: on a 2-hour Hindi stream a Make run took 197 s with correct lines like "poori mod di yaar, kya bhai? arre pulis". The local "Accurate (turbo)" model was removed because its captions were worse. The only local model left on purpose is **Best Hindi (large-v3, slow)**. Videos without YouTube captions (local files, Twitch VODs) still need a local model as the only option; expect rougher captions there, or import an .srt.

## Style & extras

- **Templates:** wrap the clip in an *X post* (light or dark), a *TikTok hook* box or a *Breaking news* broadcast frame. Type the name, handle and hook; the card, avatar letter, check mark and ticker are drawn for you.
- **Background card:** padded, rounded-corner video card on a blurred copy, a colour, a gradient or your own image (dimmed, blurred).
- **Logo / watermark** (4 corners, size, opacity), **credit line** (or "Clip: channel name" automatically), **outro ribbon** that slides in for the last seconds.
- **Music bed:** one track under the voice that rises to a peak volume in the last seconds (volume, peak and riser length are yours).
- **Six caption animations:** highlight (word by word), pop-in, pop-in line, one by one, build up, full line.
- **Import captions:** drop an `.srt` or `.ass` file; the words are timed to the clip and can be edited.
- All of it works in Make clips, single exports and "Edit saved clips" (including "apply to all clips of this video").

## Find my facecam

The **Find my facecam** chip (or "find it automatically when I press Make clips") looks at 14 frames of the video, finds rectangles whose border stays in the same place, and keeps the one that holds a face (small local YuNet face model, MIT licence, `models/`). It rejects the game's minimap and HUD panels, finds webcams in a corner or floating on a side, and answers "no facecam" when it is not sure. Measured on 30 real saved streams: found the webcam on every stream that has one; clean "not found" on trailers and talking-head videos. Not perfect: some boxes cover only the face inside a framed webcam.

## Long streams with a free chatbot

**AI parts** (below step 01): paste a YouTube link, NeonClipping splits the video's captions into ~25-minute parts and gives a copy-ready prompt per part. Paste each into any free chatbot, paste all answers back (JSON or lines like `12:30-13:10 title`), tick the moments and press Make clips: only those sections are downloaded and rendered. A chatbot given a 9-hour transcript in one go only reads the start; small parts fix that. Nothing is sent anywhere by NeonClipping; the chatbot step is manual.

## Report a problem (English + Hindi)

The **Report a problem · समस्या बताएँ** button (bottom-right) explains, in English and Hindi, three ways to tell the maintainer what broke. You choose how much to share and **nothing is sent unless you press a button**:

| Option | What happens | Who sees it |
|---|---|---|
| **1 · GitHub issue (safest)** | Opens a pre-filled issue; you read it and press Submit yourself | Public on GitHub |
| **2 · Download diagnostics** | Saves a text file; you send it yourself (GitHub, Instagram DM, WhatsApp) | Only who you send it to |
| **3 · Send directly (optional)** | After you tick a box next to the exact text shown, posts it to the maintainer's collector | The maintainer only |

What the text contains: tool versions (app, Python, Windows, ffmpeg, yt-dlp), the recent error messages with a short label such as `youtube-bot-check`, and your note if you wrote one. Video links (only the site name stays), user names in paths, e-mails, IP addresses and token-like values are removed before anything is shown, logged or shared. No videos, transcripts, cookies or browser data are ever read. Failed jobs are also written to `data/errors.log` on your own computer (redacted, trimmed automatically); that file never leaves the computer unless you share it.

Option 3 stays off ("not set up") until a collector URL is configured; see [`tools/report-worker`](tools/report-worker/README.md). Code: [`report.py`](report.py), [`report.js`](report.js). Issue form: `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/problem.yml`.

## Source quality (1080p default, 4K optional)

Under **Resolution** there is a **Source quality** menu: how sharp the video is that gets downloaded from YouTube. It used to be fixed at 720p, which made 1080p/4K exports upscaled and soft. Now:

| Choice | What you get | Measured (20 s section of a 4K video) |
|---|---|---|
| **1080p (default)** | H.264 1920x1080 | 10 MB |
| 4K | AV1/VP9 3840x2160, much larger, slower to decode | 70 MB |
| 1440p | in between | |
| 720p | fastest, smallest | 6 MB |

If a video only exists at 720p on YouTube (some new uploads and low-quality sources), you get 720p whatever you choose. **Resolution** (export size) is a separate setting: for a sharp 4K export pick Source quality 4K and Resolution 2160. Imports are cached per link and re-downloaded if you later ask for a higher quality.

## "Sign in to confirm you're not a bot" (YouTube bot check)

Some connections get this from YouTube: shared or mobile-data internet, VPNs, office/hostel Wi-Fi, or an old downloader. NeonClipping handles it for you in this order, with no setup:

1. **Keeps yt-dlp fresh.** Once a day at start-up it upgrades `yt-dlp[default]` (offline-safe). Turn off with `NEONCLIPPING_NO_AUTOUPDATE=1`.
2. **Retries in other YouTube modes** (TV, Safari, iOS, mobile web clients) instead of failing on the first block.
3. **Shows one short message** with the fixes below instead of a long English error.

If YouTube still blocks you, pick one:

| Fix | How |
|---|---|
| **Upload the MP4** | Use **Upload video** next to the link box. Always works. |
| **Use your browser login** | Sign in to YouTube in Chrome (or Edge / Firefox / Brave), then start NeonClipping with `NEONCLIPPING_COOKIES_BROWSER=chrome`. PowerShell: `$env:NEONCLIPPING_COOKIES_BROWSER='chrome'; ./run.ps1`. Close the browser first if Windows says the cookie file is locked. |
| **Use a cookies file** | Export `cookies.txt` from your browser and save it as `data/youtube_cookies.txt` (or point `NEONCLIPPING_COOKIES_FILE` at it). It stays on your computer. |
| **Change network** | Home Wi-Fi instead of mobile data; turn the VPN off. |

Cookies are only read when you set one of the options above; NeonClipping never reads your browser by itself. Use a throw-away Google account if you do not want your main one attached to automated downloads. Python 3.10 is deprecated by yt-dlp: use Python 3.11+ so updates keep arriving. Everything YouTube-related goes through [`ytdl.py`](ytdl.py).

## Honest limits

- Highlight picking is a heuristic plus a small local LLM. It finds loud, energetic, quotable moments, not guaranteed "viral" ones. Review before posting.
- The action cues (motion, flash, light flicker) are simple heuristics on a tiny low-resolution copy; they rank moments, they do not recognise "a police chase". Star ratings are how it gets better at your taste.
- The LLM sees text only. It cannot see the screen.
- Without YouTube captions (Twitch VODs, uploaded files) a speech model must transcribe each candidate, which is slow on CPU.
- Auto-caption accuracy follows the source: YouTube's auto captions are imperfect, especially Hinglish.
- Deep mode was verified on a short video only; on multi-hour videos it downloads the whole file first and is slow by design.
- **Live clipping:** one live session at a time, and the computer must stay awake and online while it records. Unattended creator-watch sessions stop after 3 hours or when less than 8 GB of disk is free (both configurable above); a manual session does not.
- **No auto-posting or scheduling.** NeonClipping exports the MP4 and SRT to your computer and stops there on purpose: posting to Instagram/YouTube/TikTok needs your accounts and approved API access, which would break "no account, nothing leaves your computer". Upload with the platform's own app or a scheduler you trust.
- **Caption languages:** Hinglish, Hindi, English and 50 more (Whisper). Accuracy is best for widely spoken languages. Captions are drawn with fonts installed on your computer, so scripts without a font may show empty boxes, and right-to-left languages (Arabic, Persian, Hebrew, Urdu) have basic support only. When YouTube provides captions in the spoken language they are used instead of the speech model.
- Facecam presets are starting points, not detection: if you pick Bottom-right but the cam is bottom-left, the top half of the clip will show the wrong area. Pick the right corner or draw your own boxes.

## Support

NeonClipping is free. If it saves you time you can ⭐ star the repo, follow [@iamajmeena](https://www.instagram.com/iamajmeena/), or optionally donate via Razorpay (UPI / cards): <https://rzp.io/rzp/JN41CpW>. The app also has a ♥ Donate button. Nothing is ever locked behind a donation.

## Credits and inspiration

Design ideas studied from open-source clippers: [PeakCut](https://github.com/haziqahmedqasmi/PeakCut) (audio-first download, captions as transcript, section download), [ClipCutter](https://github.com/curtyo18/ClipCutter), [content-ai](https://github.com/buddah0/content-ai), and the Growlance live-clipper script. Also studied: PeakCut's facecam-by-static-border idea and creator list (reimplemented here with our own code, plus a face check), the public feature list of the YIZERGE desktop editor (templates, background card, music riser, caption animations; only its public web page was read), and a creator's walkthrough of splitting a 9-hour stream into small transcript parts for a free chatbot. Built on FFmpeg, yt-dlp, FastAPI, faster-whisper, OpenCV (YuNet face detector, MIT), Ollama.

## License

MIT. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).

## What changed on 2026-11-21

- **Download quality next to Get preview.** 1080p is the default; choose 4K, 1440p or 720p right beside the button. The 1080p setting no longer falls back to YouTube's ready-made 720p mp4, and the progress line shows video/audio stream, MB, speed and time left.
- **Very long videos (over 2 hours) are never downloaded whole.** A 24-hour stream is about 46 GB at 1080p. You pick the part (up to 2 hours, h:mm:ss) and only that part is downloaded.
- **Opening heading on/off** (*Show opening heading on the clip*, on by default). Off means no heading text, no backing box and no local-model call.
- **Fixes for reported install problems:** PyAV 19 (`metadata_errors`) shim and `av<19` pin, portable FFmpeg fallback and an on-screen warning when FFmpeg is missing, Windows installer uses Python 3.10 to 3.13 and installs the Visual C++ runtime when `ctranslate2.dll` cannot load, a live "working…" line while long audio is scanned.
- **Report a problem** is now also in the sidebar and header.
- On NVIDIA PCs the source is also decoded on the GPU (NVDEC), with automatic fallback to the CPU. Task Manager shows this under *Video Encode / Video Decode*, not under *3D*.

## Updating

NeonClipping now updates itself. When a new version is on GitHub, a green banner appears at the top of the page; press **Update now**, or leave it and it updates automatically after a short countdown when nothing is running. Your clips, settings and downloaded models are kept, one backup of the replaced files stays in `.update-backup/`, and the app restarts by itself.

If you installed an older version, run `NeonClipping-Setup.bat` once more to get this feature. After that no re-install is needed. A git checkout is never touched by the updater (use `git pull`).

## Look and feel of the opening heading

Pick **Heading look** in step 04: *Impact* (default: big bold text, one accent word, pop-in, pink underline), *Neon glow*, *Banner bar* or the classic rounded box. Every finished clip also has a **Cover image** (a sharp frame with the title) and the clips ZIP includes it. See [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) for everything that changed.

## Cloud AI (optional)

A slow PC without a GPU can use a cloud model instead of Ollama for scoring moments and writing titles and hooks. Open **Cloud AI (optional)** on the page, pick a provider (Groq, OpenRouter, Gemini, OpenAI or LM Studio), paste your key, press **Test connection**, tick **Use Cloud AI** and Save. Only the *text* of candidate clips is sent to your provider; videos, audio and frames never leave your PC. The key is stored in `data/llm.json` on your computer and is never shown again. Speech-to-text still uses YouTube's captions or the local model. Environment variables `NEONCLIPPING_LLM_BASE_URL`, `NEONCLIPPING_LLM_MODEL` and `NEONCLIPPING_LLM_KEY` also work.

items.readme: # Xbox Emulator **Running the Xbox Series X|S library on PC. A continuation of [drycheetah84/TomBox](https://github.com/drycheetah84/TomBox).** The runtime reimplements the console's platform layer (Xbox-flavoured Direct3D 12, precompiled RDNA2 shaders, unified-memory textures, system libraries) so dumped, already-decrypted Xbox Series X|S builds run as normal Windows processes. It is not tied to any single title. This repo tracks our continuation — new titles brought up, platform calls extended, shader stages unlocked. Uses legally obtained, already-decrypted dumps. The runtime does no key extraction or package decryption. **Source code:** the emulator's Rust workspace is in this repo: [`crates/`](crates/), [`tools/`](tools/) and `Cargo.toml`. It contains no game files, binaries or build output. **Contributing:** pull requests are welcome, especially console library functions still marked missing in the [library map](docs/LIBRARY_MAP.md). See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). Licensed GPL-3.0-or-later (see [LICENSE](LICENSE)). Releases before this change remain available under MIT OR Apache-2.0. ## Status [![system functions](docs/img/badge-imports.svg)](docs/img/progress.svg) [![Direct3D 12.x methods](docs/img/badge-d3d12x.svg)](docs/img/progress.svg) [![RDNA2 instructions](docs/img/badge-instructions.svg)](docs/img/progress.svg) [![shaders translated](docs/img/badge-shaders.svg)](#tested-titles) [![shader stages](docs/img/badge-stages.svg)](docs/img/progress.svg) [![milestones](docs/img/badge-milestones.svg)](#milestones) [![titles examined](docs/img/badge-titles.svg)](#tested-titles) [![Xbox console libraries](docs/img/badge-console.svg)](docs/LIBRARY_MAP.md) [![progress map](docs/img/progress.svg)](docs/img/progress.svg) One square per item. items.description: GTA VI static recompilation research for x64 Windows. Source-built EXEs run on Windows, and two translated pixel shaders match reference outputs on hardware and WARP. Full-game startup is unverified.
items.readme:
# Xbox2Windows

Xbox2Windows researches static recompilation from Xbox Series X|S (Scarlett) to x64 Windows. It translates selected x64 machine code into C++ and selected gfx1013 shaders into desktop DXIL. The public tests build their own inputs and run without a game installation.

**Startup status.** Source-built Windows programs run from entry to process exit. The main executable was absent from the inspected package. Execution of the title's CPU code, full-game startup and frame rate remain unverified.

[Results](#current-results-and-open-work) · [Coverage chart](#instruction-coverage) · [Community and contributions](#community-and-contributions) · [Build on Windows](#first-build) · [Choose an experiment](#choose-an-experiment) · [Run the GPU check](#run-the-gpu-check)

## Current results and open work

| What runs | What was compared |
|---|---|
| **x64 programs from PE entry** | A two-record archive reader runs with blast 1.3 decompression under Windows, the PE mapper and the recompiled build. The three agree on output bytes, callback order, completed records, allocations, releases and exit status, including truncation and a refused output window. [Reproduce the archive comparison](docs/experiments.md#recompiling-the-blast-decoder) |
| **Raster draw from PE entry** | The shim-startup EXE reuses one D3D12 texture across three 64×64 draws, including a partial compute update and a pipeline change. Native, mapped and recompiled runs match all 16,384 RGBA bytes per frame. A skipped update is detected at the first stale pixel. A second fixture uploads an 8x8 RGBA8 and a mode-6 BC7 texture from the CPU and samples them through a vertex-buffer quad, byte-exact across the three runners, with half-texel-UV and corrupted-upload negative controls. [Reproduce the draw comparison](docs/experiments.md#exe-startup-through-the-desktop-runtime-shims) |
| **Pixel shaders** | At `c849f7a`, 851 of 12,101 PS records compiled, built D3D12 pipelines and matched controlled output on RTX 4060 Laptop and WARP. A two-mip draw verifies explicit LOD 0. A separate probe follows a constant-buffer read shared by 529 blocked records. Swapping buffers changes all 1,024 probe pixels. [Color readback](docs/experiments.md#offline-pixel-shader-recompilation) · [Depth and bindings](docs/experiments.md#buffered-depth-export) · [Read probe and latest counts](docs/experiments.md#first-unresolved-constant-buffer-read) |
| **Compute shaders** | Of 2,689 package records, 12 ran under the tested UAV bindings. Each adapter passed 14 full-buffer comparisons, including dispatches with different group counts. [Dispatch and readback](docs/experiments.md#compute-uav-stores-from-a-native-container) |
| **Mesh shaders** | A specialized entry fetched indexed vertices from a GPU buffer. Two position sets covered 1,024 and 276 pixels on a 32×32 target, matching the CPU reference on hardware and WARP. A compute and vertex fallback also draws the source-built indexed triangle on GTX 1060 and Windows 10 in-box WARP. [Mesh draw and specialization limits](docs/experiments.md#single-group-mesh-entry-specialization) · [SM 6.0 fallback](docs/experiments.md#mesh-draw-fallback) |
| **Windows runtime** | Bink frame-buffer allocations reach the Windows heap through the shared provider. The FidelityFX experiment follows scratch writes from two passes through the RCAS output on an 8×4 tile. [Allocation, failure and retry](docs/experiments.md#frame-buffers-through-the-shared-windows-heap) · [Upscaler pixel comparison](docs/experiments.md#last-writers-of-the-pass-26-scratch-reads) |

### Instruction coverage

The chart counts instruction forms exercised by passing source-built fixtures. The experiments above measure program outputs and package shader records.

![Instruction forms exercised by the latest published Windows CI fixtures](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/refs/heads/coverage-dashboard/dashboard.svg)

Both Windows jobs on `main` must pass before CI publishes a new chart. The image shows the measured commit and run ID.

[Chart source commit and CI run](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/tree/coverage-dashboard#instruction-coverage) · [Find forms without a passing fixture](CONTRIBUTING.md#share-a-reproducible-finding)

## Community and contributions

- **Claim a task.** Search for the behavior or test name in [open issues](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues) and [open PRs](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/pulls). On the issue, say what you will test, on which platform, and which shared interface or other PR your work depends on. For a first patch, start with [good first issues](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3A%22good+first+issue%22).
- **Submit a change.** Keep the PR focused on one behavior. Link the task it advances and any prerequisite PR. Include the exact command, expected and observed results, and a negative control for a new fixture. [Patch and evidence guide](CONTRIBUTING.md#submit-and-review-a-patch)
- **Review a PR.** For CPU translation or PE loading, reproduce the comparison with the original fixture. For shaders or GPU compatibility, check the DXIL and relevant WARP or hardware results. Both reviewers cover shared CPU/GPU interfaces. Record your verdict and the commit you tested. The Maintainer merges after review threads are resolved and the required Windows check passes. [Review responsibilities](CONTRIBUTING.md#who-reviews-and-merges-a-pr)
- **Contribute a hardware result.** Run the [standalone GPU check](#run-the-gpu-check) and post the report in [issue #1](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/1). You can also claim a batch there without owning a GPU. Verify the original logs, add new adapters as rows in the [hardware table](#hardware-coverage), and link driver retests in the existing row.

[New contributor guide](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/discussions/75) · [Build and debugging Q&A](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/discussions/categories/development-q-a) · [Report a bug or propose research](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/new/choose) · [Community conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) · [Private security reports](SECURITY.md)

## First build

On x64 Windows, install Python 3.11 or newer and Visual Studio's **Desktop development with C++** workload, including x64 MSVC, CMake, Ninja, and Windows SDK 10.0.26100 with DXC. Windows CI uses Python 3.12. Open PowerShell at the repository root and run the following commands.

```powershell
.\tools\dev.ps1
python -m venv out/pe-env
.\out\pe-env\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
cmake --preset dev
cmake --build --preset dev
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R 'desktop_root_signature|era_heap_allocation|offscreen_warp'
```

The smoke tests exercise a D3D12 root signature, heap allocation and software rendering. For just those checks, you can omit the two Python setup commands. With the Python environment installed, [run a focused experiment](#choose-an-experiment) or run the full suite with `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error`.

To build and test at /O2 as Windows CI also does, use the `release` preset in place of `dev`. Its build directory is `out/build/release`.

Contributing from macOS or Linux? See the [non-Windows host guide](docs/non-windows-hosts.md) for the platform-independent Python and LLVM 15 checks.

### Windows build notes

- **DXC validation.** `shader_metadata_probe` skips when the validator lacks module-only validation. DXC 1.8.2502 is the first verified release that passes. To use a separate DXC installation, configure with `cmake --preset dev -DDXC_EXECUTABLE=C:/path/to/dxc/bin/x64/dxc.exe`. [Results by release](docs/experiments.md#module-only-validation-by-dxc-release) · [Original report](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/98) · [DXC download](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/releases/tag/v1.8.2502)
- **Windows 10.** The source-built BVH buffer operations run on in-box WARP at SM 6.0. For WARP checks that require SM 6.5 or DXR, use the app-local Agility SDK and WARP packages.
