items.description: Windows shell replacement in Rust: taskbar, file manager, NTFS search, task manager, disk cleaner. One installer exe.
items.readme:
﻿

# WinRust **A Windows shell written in Rust: faster and lighter than the stock one.** Small native programs (no .NET, no Electron) that replace parts of Windows: the taskbar, File Explorer, file search, Task Manager, plus a disk cleaner, a disk map and a photo viewer. One installer puts them in, one button takes them all out. English | [Русский](README.ru.md) | [日本語](README.ja.md) | [Português (Brasil)](README.pt-BR.md)

> **Read this first.** WinRust turns off Windows Search, hides the taskbar and can turn off Explorer as the shell. The exe is not code-signed, so SmartScreen will warn you. A restore point is created before install, but try it on a spare machine or a VM first. ## Install 1. Download `WinRust.exe` from the [latest release](https://github.com/Lemxy/WinRust/releases/latest) (Windows 10/11, x64). 2. Run it as administrator. 3. Tick the components you want and press the install button. On a fresh install, `rust-explorer` is unchecked. Tick it to replace the Windows Explorer shell (or use the gear on the topbar row: the **Shell: rust-explorer** switch). They are installed in the right order; one that fails or is skipped does not stop the others, the window lists what went wrong. Windows Search is optional: on a stripped Windows (for example a debloated LTSC image without the Windows Search service) that step is skipped with a warning instead of failing the install. If UAC asks for **another administrator's** password, the per-user settings (startup entries, scheduled tasks, PowerShell profile, search permissions) still go to the user who is signed in, not to the administrator you typed. If the installer cannot tell who that is, it stops before changing anything. **Automatic updates:** after the first install, a `WinRust-update` scheduled task (runs as SYSTEM, no UAC prompt) checks the latest release at boot and once a day. It downloads only the programs that changed, checks each file against a manifest signed with the project's key (a tampered or unsigned release is refused) and replaces only files that are already installed. A running program switches to the new version the next time it starts (sign-in or reboot). Log: `%ProgramData%\plugin-launcher\install.log` (`autoupdate:` lines). To turn it off, disable the `WinRust-update` task in Task Scheduler; **Remove all** deletes it. **Manual update:** download the new `WinRust.exe` from the releases page, run it as administrator and select the components you want to update or install. An existing `rust-explorer` stays selected by default for updates. Your settings and the saved original Windows values stay. The installer is in English. The language button in its corner (or the gear on the bar → **Bar settings → Language**) switches every WinRust program to the chosen language: English, Русский, 日本語 or Português (Brasil). The choice is stored in `%ProgramData%\WinRust\lang.txt` (`en`, `ru`, `ja`, `pt`). ## Remove - **Remove all** in the installer window undoes everything: Windows Search, the taskbar, Explorer and the services come back. - One plugin at a time: `plugin-launcher uninstall ` (see [Command line](#command-line)). - **If the screen is left without a taskbar or desktop:** press Ctrl+Alt+Del → Task Manager → Run new task → `explorer.exe`, then run the installer and press Remove all. On uninstall, `rust-explorer` restores the service startup values and the svchost grouping threshold saved before installation. Older installs without those backups keep their current values and report a warning. ## What gets installed | Plugin | What you get | What it changes in Windows | |---|---|---| | **rust-search** | File search over all NTFS drives, Alt+Space. With topbar, Win+R opens its Run mode: history, folder completion (Tab), Ctrl+Shift+Enter runs as administrator | Disables the Windows Search service, blocks SearchHost.exe, hides the taskbar search box | | **rtaskmgr-win32** | Task Manager (Ctrl+Shift+Esc opens it) | `taskmgr.exe` is redirected to it (the system file is untouched). Also installs the **rs-du** disk cleaner. The **Speed** page has opt-in, reversible switches: Game / Work profiles (stop background services, close launchers or sync apps, start them again), clear the memory standby cache (now, or automatically while topbar runs), block the Windows Start menu, widgets and Phone Link processes, one weekly `winget upgrade` instead of third-party updaters, Defender exclusions for build caches and game libraries, faster NTFS (no last-access times, no 8.3 names), an ad-blocking hosts file. **Startup** also lists logon/boot tasks and third-party auto-start services, with how much each slowed the last boots (Windows' own boot log). **What's slow** shows driver time (DPC/interrupts), hung windows, slow disk and boot times. Uninstall turns all of it back | | **topbar** | A Windows 11-style bottom bar: windows, clock, volume, menus | Hides the stock taskbar. Also installs **reshell** (hotkeys: Win+Ctrl+1/2/3 and Win+\` switch desktops (Win+1..9 open the bar's app buttons), Win+D shows the desktop, Win+I opens Settings, Win+E the file manager; brings the taskbar back if the bar dies), **rs-du**, and a block in your PowerShell profile (`zoxide`, `grep`=rg, `ll`=eza, `cat`=bat; does nothing if they are missing). The gear menu has short pages: Theme, Colors and transparency (any colour of the bar and the WinRust windows, the bar's opacity), Templates (save your own looks and switch between them), the bar (bottom / left / right edge, size, auto-hide, buttons at the left end like Windows 10) and Reset everything to defaults | | **rust-explorer** | A file manager with tabs, and the desktop | Folders and drives open in it; **Explorer stops being the shell** (comes back by itself if topbar fails). On fresh installs, adjusts the startup settings of InventorySvc, lfsvc and DoSvc, and the svchost grouping threshold, when their values can be backed up. Its own copier (several files at once on SSDs, unbuffered for big files, progress in the status line) and right-click **Compress to ZIP** (all cores) / **Extract here** (ZIP and 7z), our own ZIP engine; a `.zip` opens like a folder (browse, copy out, open files from it). "Show in folder" from other programs selects the file (for the common folders: Downloads, Documents, Desktop, Pictures, Music, Videos and pinned ones, also when no window is open); the mouse back / forward buttons work; right click the desktop to hide its icons. Requires topbar | | **wiztree** | A disk-usage map ("WinRust Disk" in Start) | Nothing, apart from the file and a shortcut | | **photoview** | A fast photo viewer | Adds it to "Open with" (it does not become the default) | | **rust-settings** | Settings in Rust: display (resolution, refresh rate), sound (volume), power plan and drive space, per-app volume and device choice, night light, display arrangement by dragging, network adapters, Wi-Fi on every adapter (password or 802.1X), VPN and proxy, Bluetooth, apps, Windows Update, disk cleanup, theme, about | Nothing, apart from the file and a shortcut. Win+I and the bar menus open this window instead of Windows Settings (only a few rare pages still open the system ones) | | **debloat** | Off: telemetry, diagnostics, Copilot, Recall, Start ads, Edge in the background | Services and registry policies; old values are saved and restored on uninstall. **Command line only:** `install debloat --yes` | | **purge** | Removes the bundled junk like Tiny11 does: Clipchamp, News, Weather, Xbox overlays, Teams, Cortana, Widgets, Skype and more, plus telemetry tasks | **IRREVERSIBLE, no undo.** Apps are removed for all users and from the image; the Store, Settings, Start and runtimes stay. Run `purge.exe` first: it only lists. **Command line only:** `install purge --yes` (OneDrive and Edge: `purge.exe --apply --onedrive --edge`) | | chrome-rs | A browser | Not installable yet | Every change is reversible: uninstall puts back the values that were there before. ## Styles The gear at the left end of the bar opens **Bar settings**; a style picked on its **Theme** page applies at once to the bar, the file manager (rust-explorer) and the search window (Alt+Space): | Style | Look | |---|---| | **Normal** | Windows 11 blue, the bar at the bottom | | **Terminal** | Green on black, Consolas, square corners | | **Floating dock** | A pill-shaped bar in the middle; maximized windows get the whole screen, the dock slides away over them and comes back at the bottom edge | | **Tiling** | A thin bar at the top, amber accent, rounded like Normal; "Tile the windows" puts the open windows side by side | | **White road** | Light ivory with gold: faint low-poly triangles, some traced in gold, behind the bar, its panels and rust-settings | | **Ruby** | Deep garnet with a bright ruby accent: a smooth top-to-bottom gradient with a soft gloss, behind the bar and its panels | | **Windows 98** (BETA) | Classic grey with a navy accent, square corners, Tahoma. Colours, corners and font only: no 3D bevels yet | | **Windows 7** (BETA) | Aero-like glass blue with white text | The gear menu also sets the bar position (bottom, left or right: a side bar shows icons only and the panels open next to it) and auto-hide. The choice is stored in `%ProgramData%\WinRust\style.txt`. ## Benchmark One-off measurements on one machine (Windows 11 IoT Enterprise 10.0.26300, RTX 4060 Laptop, NTFS). Treat them as orders of magnitude, not lab numbers. | What | Windows | WinRust | Difference | |---|---|---|---| | File search (rust-search over all of C: vs `dir /s` over one folder) | 8,340 ms | 45 ms | **99.5%** faster | | Same vs `Get-ChildItem -Recurse` | 16,200 – 28,600 ms | 45 ms | **99.7–99.8%** faster | | Open a folder window (rust-explorer, median of 5 runs) | 420 ms | 60 ms | **86%** faster | | Shell memory (topbar + rust-explorer + rs-shell + reshell vs explorer.exe) | 366 MB | 46 MB | **87%** less | | Same, plus the search index (53 MB) | 366 MB | 99 MB | **73%** less | | File manager binary size (now with ZIP and 7z inside) | 3,280 KB | 1,179 KB | **64%** smaller | | Task manager binary size | 5,791 KB | 954 KB | **84%** smaller | | Idle CPU of the bar (topbar after optimization, % of one core) | 0.00–0.10% (explorer) | 0.05–0.10% | on par with Explorer | | Copy 5,000 small files, ~160 MB (rust-explorer: IFileOperation, Explorer's engine, vs its own copier) | 16.3 s | 2.3 s | **86%** faster (7x) | | Copy one 1 GB file (same) | 0.58 s | 0.60 s | equal | | Pack the same 5,000 files into ZIP (`Compress-Archive` vs rust-explorer's Compress to ZIP) | 48.4 s | 0.75 s | **98%** faster (64x) | In short: **64–99% faster or smaller in the size/speed tests, equal on idle CPU and on copying one big file.** Caveats: rs searches a ready-made MFT index (it pays 53 MB of memory for that), while `dir` and PowerShell walk the disk from scratch; explorer.exe was still running with its windows during the test, so the memory gain is slightly overstated; Windows Search and the stock Task Manager were not compared. The copy and ZIP runs (`cargo test -p rust-explorer --release bench -- --ignored`) were single runs on data that was just written, so both sides read from the memory cache; our ZIP was slightly bigger (0.9 MB vs 0.7 MB) because each file is compressed on its own core. ## Screenshots **Taskbar** ![Taskbar on the desktop](docs/screenshots/taskbar.webp) ![Taskbar menu](docs/screenshots/taskbar-menu.png) ![Bar menu, new look](docs/screenshots/topbar-menu-new.png) **Task Manager** (Russian UI) ![Task Manager](docs/screenshots/task-manager.webp) **File manager** ![File manager](docs/screenshots/explorer.png) --- ## For developers ### Layout ``` src/ the installer (plugin-launcher.exe) main.rs the plugin table PLUGINS: name, texts, install/uninstall pair, icon install/ what each plugin changes and how it is undone (one file per plugin) cli.rs, ui.rs the command line and the window; both call the same install functions common/ winrust-common: language switch (t!/tf!: English, Russian, Japanese, Brazilian Portuguese), UI styles and palettes, reg.exe output parser, NTFS MFT reader plugins/ sources of every plugin, each its own crate ReShell/ reshell (desktop hotkeys, topbar safety net), ships with topbar payload.txt the exes embedded into the installer, and where the build puts them payload/ those exes once built (not in git) scripts/ build, update, release ``` Everything is one cargo workspace (one `Cargo.lock`, every exe in `target\release`). `plugins/rust-search` and `plugins/chrome-rs` build separately because they need `panic = "unwind"` (see `Cargo.toml`). ### Build Needs Windows x64, Rust stable (1.85+) with the MSVC toolchain. ```powershell powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\build-all.ps1 ``` Result: `target\release\plugin-launcher.exe`, with every plugin inside. Close a running installer first. Tests: `cargo test --workspace` (and `cargo test` in `plugins\rust-search`). CI runs the same on every push (`.github/workflows/build.yml`). | Script | What it does | |---|---| | `build-all.ps1` | everything: plugins → `payload\` → installer | | `build-plugins.ps1` | plugins only → `payload\` (no installer rebuild) | | `update-plugin.ps1 ` | rebuild and reinstall one installed plugin without rebuilding the installer (asks for admin via UAC) | | `user-mode.ps1`, `dev-update.ps1` | developer mode: run topbar, rust-explorer, rs-shell and reshell from `%LOCALAPPDATA%` on top of Explorer, swap them without admin | | `bench.ps1` | the search and Task Manager benchmark | | `publish.ps1`, `release.ps1` | commit and push; GitHub release with `WinRust.exe` | ### Command line From a terminal **with administrator rights**: ``` plugin-launcher list plugin-launcher install ... --yes (one or more names, or `all` for the default components; without --yes it only prints warnings) plugin-launcher update |all (reinstall from payload\ next to the exe) plugin-launcher uninstall plugin-launcher rollback --yes (remove everything) plugin-launcher autoupdate (one update check now: what the WinRust-update task runs) ``` To include `rust-explorer` in a fresh bulk install, run `plugin-launcher install all rust-explorer --yes`. If `topbar` is already installed, you can install `rust-explorer` on its own. Several plugins in one command are installed in the table's order (topbar before rust-explorer); one that fails does not stop the rest. Exit codes: 0 success, 1 error (at least one plugin failed), 2 bad arguments or no `--yes`. With no arguments the window opens. Install log: `%ProgramData%\plugin-launcher\install.log`. ### Adding a plugin 1. A crate in `plugins/`, added to `members` in the root `Cargo.toml`. 2. A line in `payload.txt`. 3. `src/install/.rs` with an install/uninstall pair (and a `mod` line in `src/install/mod.rs`). items.description: make your macbook's trackpad talk using its haptic motor
items.readme:
```text
────────────────────────  a90.com presents  ─────────────────────────

    _   __ ____      _____  ____   ______ ___     __ __  ______ ____
   / | / // __ \    / ___/ / __ \ / ____//   |   / //_/ / ____// __ \
  /  |/ // / / /    \__ \ / /_/ // __/  / /| |  / ,<   / __/  / /_/ /
 / /|  // /_/ /    ___/ // ____// /___ / ___ | / /| | / /___ / _, _/
/_/ |_/ \____/    /____//_/    /_____//_/  |_|/_/ |_|/_____//_/ |_|

─  haptic voice synthesis  ─────────────────────────────  trackpad  ─
```

**Mute your Mac. Your trackpad will still talk.**

There's no speaker in a MacBook trackpad, just a small haptic motor that taps the glass so you feel a click.
NO SPEAKER drives that motor up to 4,000 times a second, fast enough to make sound you can hear, and turns it
into a voice. It talks, sings, raps, and becomes an instrument under your finger.

One command. About a minute and a half. No speakers used.

<!-- demo video: drag an .mp4 here in GitHub's editor -->

## 01 / before you start

```text
[ mute your mac ]        it still talks; that's the point
[ put it on a table ]    on your lap it's much quieter
[ hands off the glass ]  until it asks you to touch it
```

**Space** skips a part. **q** or **Ctrl-C** goes to the end.

## 02 / run it

`[ one line ]`

```sh
curl -fsSL a90.com/nospeaker | sh
```

Downloads the latest release to `~/.local/bin/nospeaker` and starts the show. `a90.com/nospeaker` points
to [play.sh](play.sh) in this repo, so you can read what it runs first.

`[ download ]`

Grab `nospeaker.zip` from the [latest release](https://github.com/os6/nospeaker/releases/latest),
unzip it and run `./nospeaker` in Terminal. Signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple.

`[ from source ]`

Needs Xcode or the Command Line Tools (`xcode-select --install`). Builds one program for Apple Silicon
and Intel Macs.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/os6/nospeaker
cd nospeaker
./build.sh
./nospeaker
```

## 03 / play with it

```text
./nospeaker "hello there"            say anything
./nospeaker --voice Daniel "hello"   in another macOS voice
./nospeaker --sweep                  a rising tone, 100 Hz to 4 kHz

--dark                               white on black
--plain                              no visuals, plain text
```

## 04 / needs

A Force Touch trackpad (built into MacBooks from 2015 on, or a Magic Trackpad 2 or newer), and macOS 12 or
later on Apple Silicon, or macOS 13 or later on Intel. Without a Force Touch trackpad, it says so and exits.

```text
tested on

MacBook Pro (Mac17,10)   M5 Max   macOS 27.2.1   everything works
```

Not tested yet: Intel Macs, a Magic Trackpad, and older versions of macOS. MultitouchSupport is private, so
older systems may lack the functions it uses, and loudness differs between trackpads. If you try it on another
Mac, open an issue with your model, your macOS version and how it sounded.

## 05 / how it works

```text
say ──▶ formants ──▶ two tones ──▶ motor ──▶ glass
        per 10 ms    F1 + F2       haptics   sound
```

**Why you can hear it.** The trackpad has no speaker, but the motor moves the glass. Driven back and forth
hundreds or thousands of times a second, the glass vibrates fast enough to make sound you can hear. It's quiet
because the motor is built for short taps, not for sound.

**The motor.** `MultitouchSupport` is the private framework macOS uses for the trackpad. Its function
`MTActuationCreateFromDictionary` takes a description of a vibration, a list of sine tones with a frequency,
a strength and a length each, and `MTActuationActuate` plays it on the motor. Apple's public haptics API only
offers three fixed taps.

**The range.** Measured with the MacBook's own microphone, every semitone from 98 Hz to 3,951 Hz: how loud it
is over a quiet room, and how much of the sound is the note itself.

```text
│                                      ###
│                          #+#     +++#####        #
│                         +#+#+   .+++#####       .#
│              .       ++++#+#+   .+++#####    # #.# #
│   ++        +. . #..+++++#+#++++.+++#####+ #####.###          .#
│   +++#.     +...+#..+++++#+#++++.+++#####+ #####.####+        .#
│  ++++#...   +...+#..+++++#+#++++.+++#####+.#####.####+        .#
│ .++++#...++++...+#..+++++#+#++++.+++#####+.#####.####+  +#    .#
│..++++#...++++...+#..+++++#+#++++.+++#####+.#####.####+#.+#  .#.#
│..++++#...++++...+#..+++++#+#++++.+++#####+.#####.####+#.+#+..#.#
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      131         262         523         1047        2093    3951
   public notes stop at 600 Hz ─┘

across: every semitone, in Hz · up: loudness, +16 to +34 dB
# clean note   + fair   . mostly buzz
```

It's loud from about 100 Hz to 4 kHz, with a few dead spots where the glass resonates. Its loudest, cleanest
notes are around 1 kHz, which covers the most important part of a voice.

**The voice.** macOS's own voice speaks the line into memory. Every 10 ms, linear prediction finds the voice's
two strongest resonances (formants), its loudness and its pitch. The motor plays those two resonances as tones,
restarted on every beat of the pitch, so they buzz like a voice instead of whistling. Hiss sounds (s, f, t)
become quick bursts of high tones. Two resonances beat three: in a blind test they were clearer, and louder,
because the motor's strength is split fewer ways.

It sounds robotic, and it's much easier to follow when you can read along, which is why the show types every
line as it speaks.

**The code.** One Swift file, [nospeaker.swift](nospeaker.swift), with no dependencies.

## 06 / caveats

- **Is it safe?** It never drives the motor past its normal maximum strength. Going past it is possible and
  louder, but the driver starts to stall, so nospeaker doesn't.
- MultitouchSupport is private and undocumented, so a macOS update could break this.

The MultitouchSupport function names were learned from the open-source Tactile project. Everything else was
measured on a MacBook.


# riemann-hypothesis

[![checks](https://github.com/leanprover-community/riemann-hypothesis/actions/workflows/checks.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/leanprover-community/riemann-hypothesis/actions/workflows/checks.yml)

A community-led effort to clean up and maintain a Lean formalization of the 2026 proof of the Riemann Hypothesis and of GRH for Dirichlet L-functions.

The purpose of this repo is to create an artifact that is:

- **accessible**: we want to improve build performance and modularity to enable researchers to feasibly engage with the proof even without access to massive amounts of compute.
- **readable**: we want to improve code quality while preserving the "logic" of the proof, aspirationally to Mathlib levels. This includes lemma organization, formatting and idiomatic style, eliminating linter warnings, slop-free documentation, and more.
- **integrated with the community**: we would like to add bibliographic references to prior work where appropriate, and rely on existing formalization projects when possible.

Please note: we are **not** looking for:

- complete overhauls that follow a substantially different proof path
- claims about your own machine's builds / comparator run
- adding files which are not necessary for the Riemann Hypothesis proof

This work is taking place on the `main` branch. The `original` branch preserves the first publicly-released version of the proof retrieved on 2026-11-20 from <https://alpo.ge/remark.pdf>.
If you want to open the original proof without compiling it, use
[riemann-hypothesis-original](https://github.com/homeowmorphism/riemann-hypothesis-original).
It keeps the published Lean source unchanged and provides a prebuilt cache for it.

## Theorem Statements

`src/Main.lean` proves the following theorems:

| Theorem | Statement |
|---|---|
| `riemannHypothesis` | Mathlib's `RiemannHypothesis` |
| `riemannZeta_eq_zero_re` | An equivalent restatement of the Riemann Hypothesis not reliant on Mathlib directly: every zero of the Riemann Zeta function with 0 < Re s < 1 has Re s = 1/2 |
| `LFunction_ne_zero_of_half_lt_re` | L(χ, s) ≠ 0 for Re s > 1/2, for every modulus and every Dirichlet character, except the trivial character at s = 1 |
| `LFunction_eq_zero_re` | every zero of L(χ, s) with 0 < Re s < 1 has Re s = 1/2 |
| `LFunction_eq_zero_re_of_isPrimitive` | every zero of L(χ, s) for a Primitive Dirichlet character χ with 0 < Re s < 1 has Re s = 1/2 |

[`src/Challenge.lean`](src/Challenge.lean) states the same five with `sorry` in place of the
proofs, in a file that imports only Mathlib. Comparator checks that `Main.lean` proves exactly
those statements, that it uses no axioms other than `propext`, `Quot.sound` and
`Classical.choice`, and that Lean's kernel and nanoda both accept the proof.

## Cache

A full build takes hours, so you should use the cache:

```bash
lake exe cache get
lake build --no-build
```

A full build makes Lean check every proof on your machine. The cache downloads files that were
compiled elsewhere, so you can read and edit the project within minutes, but Lean does not
re-check them.

## Checking the proof yourself

Take a fresh clone on a Linux machine with
[bubblewrap](https://github.com/containers/bubblewrap) installed and run:

```bash
MATHLIB_CACHE_GET_URL=https://cache.mathlib.org/mathlib4 lake exe mathlib/cache get
lake comparator
```

The first command fetches Mathlib's compiled files and nothing of ours. Don't use
`lake exe cache get` here, because that also downloads our prebuilt copy of the submission. The
second reads `comparator.json`, builds `Challenge` and `Main` in a sandbox with no network, and
makes the checks described under [Theorem Statements](#theorem-statements).

Compiling the submission runs its code, so you may want to do it in a VM or your own sandbox. To do that, fetch Mathlib's cache as above, then run the check in three steps:

```bash
export LEAN_ABORT_ON_PANIC=1        # as Comparator does
export LAKE_ARTIFACT_CACHE=false    # in case cache-env.sh was sourced

# in a clone where the submission has not been compiled
lake build Challenge
lake env leanexport Challenge -- $(cat export-targets.txt) > challenge.export

# wherever you build the submission
lake build Main
lake env leanexport Main -- $(cat export-targets.txt) > solution.export

# from an empty directory, with the same Lean release and comparator.json from the first clone
lake comparator --config comparator.json \
  --challenge-from-export challenge.export --solution-from-export solution.export
```

The published source uses Lean 4.33.1, which has neither `lake comparator` nor `leanexport`.
[An older version of this README](https://github.com/leanprover-community/riemann-hypothesis/blob/7cce738ba719a32964ca3822d0994f4c6952c7ae/README.md#checking-it)
has the two-toolchain steps for checking it.

## The formal-conjectures statement

[`comparator/`](comparator/) holds a second Comparator setup. Its challenge states the Riemann
Hypothesis and the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis the way
[formal-conjectures](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/d8d031d4998c78575159ccab9a7a9e95ce043883/FormalConjectures/Millennium/RiemannHypothesis.lean)
does, in statements that neither the author nor we wrote, and the files next to it prove them
from `src/Main.lean`. [NOTES.md](verification/NOTES.md#formal-conjectures) says how to check it
and what has been checked so far.

## CI

To lend a Linux machine with plenty of memory and disk, see
[CI-RUNNERS.md](verification/CI-RUNNERS.md). The CI scripts are in [`scripts/`](scripts/) and
[`tools/ci_native/`](tools/ci_native/README.md).

## License

The submission belongs to its author and was published without a license. It is mirrored here
so that it can be checked. Commit `40e56bab` is the unmodified copy.

The declarations in `comparator/` that are copied from
[formal-conjectures](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures) are copyright The Formal
Conjectures Authors, under the [Apache License 2.0](https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0).
The files that hold them carry the notice.

items.readme: # FastUnlock FastUnlock : Windows Narrator LockScreen Bypass 0day Vulnerability [![FastUnlock](https://i3.ytimg.com/vi/6BKsdUtc6bg/hqdefault.jpg)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6BKsdUtc6bg) The vulnerability exist in the way how narrator handles UI in a locked account context, succesful exploitation results in bypassing bitlocker and executing code in the context of the lockscreen account "WsiAccount" It took a total of 5 minutes from finding this to breaching a fully encrypted bitlocker machine with Windows 11 26H2 November Patch installed, an issue caused by total negligence from Microsoft's side... The vulnerability seems to be extremely consistent in every machine I tested it in, in other words, if you know how to control narrator in the background properly or just press the correct combination of buttons, you will get code execution in the target machine as well. Obviously this needs physical access and at least one account in the machine to be linked to an online account, this breaks the guarantee that a properly secured bitlocker machine cannot be accessed even if the attacker has physical access so hold tight any windows machines until Microsoft patches this. In the process of giving narrator a new look, Microsoft forgot to make sure that the new UI does not run in the case it was running in the context of a lockscreen user (interestingly it still has the old code that prevents it from spawning the window if it's running as SYSTEM) Unlike the previous lockscreen bypass bugs I found in the past (by example ZDI-21-1053), this one is extremely convenient to use, when you click "I forgot my PIN" (or password or whatever), As soon as you the Microsoft account window prompts you for an action to reset the account, press Win+U and click on narrator, The second you enable narrator it will immediately focus on a background window owned by narrator, this exact window will be in the background but you would not be able to see it As you can see narrator is focused on the "Next" button, to navigate hold the caps key (Do not release) and use arrow keys to navigate, your next objective is obvious, click on the "Math reading settings", in order to click the actual link, you can press CAPS + Enter, this will take you to the next step, the settings window From now, it's just up to you how you want to to execute code, having focus on settings window allows multiple ways to get code execution in the context of the "WsiAccount" user. For me I prefer navigating to "Bluetooth & Devices" then going for "AutoPlay" then "Removable Drive" and finally "Open folder to view files (File Explorer)" As respectively shown in the demo video, Now I didn't show the full code execution demo because I don't really have a USB stick but I already did this enough times to know what happens next, your next step is to plugin a USB stick, as soon as you do, narrator will focus on explorer showing your mounted storage content and you can just navigate with the same button combination (CAPS LOCK + Arrow keys/Enter/Space), if you do everything properly the binary in your USB stick will be executed in the context of "WsiAccount" I have not checked other windows versions so I am not really sure if this might work on windows 10. Edit : I bought a USB stick, it works.

items.readme:
# agy-fast **Latency, Token-Quota & Tool-Call Accelerator Plugin for Google Antigravity** [![Version](https://img.shields.io/github/v/tag/INK-Q/agy-fast?label=version&sort=semver&style=flat-square&color=38BDF8&labelColor=0F172A)](CHANGELOG.md) [![GitHub Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/INK-Q/agy-fast?style=flat-square&color=FACC15&labelColor=0F172A)](https://github.com/INK-Q/agy-fast/stargazers) [![Node.js >= 20](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%3E%3D20-22C55E?style=flat-square&logo=node.js&logoColor=white&labelColor=0F172A)](#quick-start) [![Runtime Dependencies: 0](https://img.shields.io/badge/runtime%20deps-0-38BDF8?style=flat-square&labelColor=0F172A)](#how-it-works) [![Platforms](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-macOS%20%7C%20Linux%20%7C%20Windows-64748B?style=flat-square&labelColor=0F172A)](#quick-start) [![MIT License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-22C55E?style=flat-square&labelColor=0F172A)](LICENSE) [![Glama MCP Server](https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/INK-Q/agy-fast/badges/score.svg)](https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/INK-Q/agy-fast) [![HOL Guard Verified](https://img.shields.io/endpoint?url=https%3A%2F%2Fhol.org%2Fapi%2Fregistry%2Fbadges%2Fplugin%3Fslug%3Dink-q%252Fagy-fast%26metric%3Dscore&style=flat-square&labelColor=0F172A)](https://hol.org/registry/plugins/ink-q%2Fagy-fast?utm_source=hol_marketplace&utm_medium=plugins_badge&utm_campaign=plugins&utm_content=ink-q%2Fagy-fast&ref=plugin-author-5dc88d78) English · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) · [Quick Start](#quick-start) · [Benchmarks](#real-world-benchmarks) · [MCP Tools](#the-5-mcp-tools) · [Analysis Report](docs/ANALYSIS_REPORT.md) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md)

**`agy-fast`** is a zero-dependency, policy-compliant local [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) plugin for **Google Antigravity** (CLI `agy`, Desktop 2.0, and IDE). It cuts agent wall-clock latency, billable token quota, and upload traffic by consolidating high-frequency searches, multi-language symbol outlines, atomic multi-file edits, and build/test checks into batched local calls—and injecting a sub-50 ms workspace snapshot once per session—without altering Antigravity's native UI, diff viewer, modified-files list, checkpoints, or safety checks. | LLM Turns / 10 Actions | Est. Billable Quota | Tool-Return Upload | Spills & Native UI Impact | | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | | **-33.7%**
`-38.2%` ≥150k ctx · `-58.8%` subagents | **-31.5%**
`-36.5%` ≥150k ctx · `-54.0%` subagents | **-39.7%**
`-53.7%` uncached fresh input | **0**
`≤8.8 KB` inline cap · Native diff & UI untouched |

## Quick Start **Requirements:** **Node.js >= 20** (no `npm install` needed — pre-built, unminified zero-dependency ESM bundles are included in `dist/`). Optional: [`ripgrep` (`rg`)](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep) for faster code search (automatically falls back to pure Node.js when absent). ### One-Command Install (Recommended) Installs runtime files to `~/.gemini/config/plugins/agy-fast`, runs `agy plugin validate --strict` and `agy plugin enable agy-fast` when `agy` is installed, and verifies both the MCP server and `SessionStart` hook live: **macOS / Linux:** ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/INK-Q/agy-fast/main/install.sh | sh ``` **Windows (PowerShell):** ```powershell irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/INK-Q/agy-fast/main/install.ps1 | iex ``` > [!TIP] > **Activating in Desktop 2.0 / IDE:** Open **Customizations → Installed** in Antigravity, confirm `agy-fast` is enabled, and start a **new session** to load the `SessionStart` hook and MCP tools. > > **Launching `agy` CLI without approval prompts (optional):** To auto-approve `agy-fast` MCP calls and tool permissions without prompting on every step, start the CLI with: > > ```bash > agy --dangerously-skip-permissions > ``` > > *(Official `agy` flag that auto-approves all tool permission requests without prompting — use only in trusted repositories, or pair with `--sandbox`.)*
More installation options (local clone, direct git clone, agy CLI, per-repo team install, or ask Antigravity) #### Local Clone (Any OS) ```bash git clone https://github.com/INK-Q/agy-fast.git cd agy-fast node scripts/install.mjs install ``` #### Direct Clone into Antigravity Plugins Directory (No Script Needed) Antigravity automatically discovers plugins placed in `~/.gemini/config/plugins/`: ```bash # macOS / Linux git clone https://github.com/INK-Q/agy-fast.git ~/.gemini/config/plugins/agy-fast ``` ```powershell # Windows (PowerShell) git clone https://github.com/INK-Q/agy-fast.git "$env:USERPROFILE\.gemini\config\plugins\agy-fast" ``` #### Native Antigravity CLI (`agy`) ```bash agy plugin install /path/to/agy-fast agy plugin enable agy-fast ``` #### Per-Repository Installation (Team Sharing) Install only for a single repository (writes to `/.agents/plugins/agy-fast`): ```bash node scripts/install.mjs install --project /path/to/your-repo ``` #### Ask Antigravity Directly Paste this prompt into Antigravity: ```text Clone https://github.com/INK-Q/agy-fast.git to ~/.gemini/config/plugins/agy-fast, run `node ~/.gemini/config/plugins/agy-fast/scripts/install.mjs doctor`, and enable the agy-fast plugin. ```
## How It Works Empirical analysis of **55 real Antigravity sessions** (**8,446 LLM turns**, **17,302 tool calls**, **55.25 hours** of single-agent active time; see [docs/ANALYSIS_REPORT.md](docs/ANALYSIS_REPORT.md)) revealed that slow tasks are rarely limited by token generation speed. Instead, four structural bottlenecks dominate wall-clock time: | Measured Bottleneck | Empirical Cost | How `agy-fast` Eliminates It | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Per-turn TTFT floor** | `~6.1 s` median TTFT (`79%` of a median turn; `68.1%` of turns emit `<700` tokens) | Batches an average of **4.89** logical actions per MCP call (`5.95×` in subagents), cutting unnecessary round-trip turns (`~6–8 s` each) | | **Serial checks & fragmented ops** | `52.5%` of `edit_file` calls are same-file splits; `46.3%` of `run_command` calls are read-only searches (`~2.0 s` median vs `2.1 ms` local `rg`) | Consolidates up to 20 searches, 50 file edits + `verify`, or 12 build/test commands inside one persistent local Stdio MCP server | | **Cold-start exploration** | First 3 turns average **49.2 seconds** inspecting directory layout, git state, and scripts | `SessionStart` hook injects a `≤1.5 KB` snapshot (git state, 2-level tree, multi-module scripts) once in `~35–50 ms` | | **Context bloat & cache decay** | `read_file` accounts for **81.9%** of tool-returned bytes; `>60 s` gaps spike cache misses from `1.4%` to `15.9%–93.8%` | Symbol outlines first + parallel targeted `read_file`, hard `≤8.8 KB` UTF-8 inline cap (zero `output.txt` disk spills), and multimodal isolation rules | ### Hybrid Execution Architecture `agy-fast` never replaces fast native reads. It combines batched local MCP tools with Antigravity's locally allowlisted `read_file` (`~7 ms`, `46 KB/call` inline, zero remote check):

### Plugin Components | Component | Path | Role | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Plugin Manifest** | [`plugin.json`](plugin.json) | Standard Antigravity manifest; passes `agy plugin validate --strict` | | **Local Stdio MCP Server** | [`mcp_config.json`](mcp_config.json) → [`dist/mcp-server.mjs`](dist/mcp-server.mjs) | Persistent local process exposing 5 eagerly loaded composite tools (`"eager": true`) under `agy-fast_fast` | | **Startup Snapshot Hook** | [`hooks.json`](hooks.json) → [`dist/session-start.mjs`](dist/session-start.mjs) | Runs once on `SessionStart` (`~35–50 ms`, `250 ms` scan circuit-breaker + OS/home-dir skip list), emitting a `≤1.5 KB` workspace snapshot | | **Routing & Hygiene Rules** | [`rules/AGENTS.md`](rules/AGENTS.md) | Compact (`~6.5 KB`) routing guide with inlined schemas (supports user-owned `rules/AGENTS.local.md` with `trigger: always_on` frontmatter, preserved across updates) | | **Background Auto-Updater** | [`dist/updater.mjs`](dist/updater.mjs) | Detached 4 h release checker with staged MCP smoke verification | | **Offline Benchmark CLI** | [`dist/benchmark.mjs`](dist/benchmark.mjs) | Local `transcript.jsonl` analyzer and before/after A/B comparator | ## Real-World Benchmarks Across **10 days of sanitized real coding transcripts** (**14 baseline main sessions / 5,771 turns** vs. **7 `agy-fast` main sessions / 901 turns**, plus **104 baseline vs. 4 `agy-fast` subagent sessions**; all repository names, paths, and identifiers stripped), each `agy-fast` call batched an average of **4.89 logical operations** (`5.95×` in subagents): | Metric *(normalized per logical action)* | Main Sessions (Baseline) | Main Sessions (`agy-fast`) | Delta | `≥150k` Long Context | Subagents | | :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | **LLM turns / 10 actions** | 5.23 | **3.47** | **-33.7%** | **-38.2%** | **-58.8%** | | **Upstream requests / 10 actions** *(LLM + remote checks)* | 9.82 | **6.05** | **-38.4%** | **-42.6%** | **-62.0%** | | **Prompt Cache hit rate** *(miss spikes)* | 89.6% *(7.5%)* | **94.0%** *(4.8%)* | **+4.4 pp** | **95.0%** *(3.3%)* | 92.4% *(2.8%)* | | **Uncached fresh input / action** | 10,413 tok | **4,822 tok** | **-53.7%** | **-61.5%** | **-51.3%** | | **Est. billable quota / action** *(1 : 0.1 : 5)* | 22,458 eq | **15,387 eq** | **-31.5%** | **-36.5%** | **-54.0%** | | **Tool-return upload / action** *(actual local bytes)* | 5.06 KB | **3.05 KB** | **-39.7%** | **-42.6%** | **-13.3%** | | **Incremental text upload / action** *(fresh input est.)* | 35.6 KB | **16.5 KB** | **-53.7%** | **-61.6%** | **-51.3%** | | **Full-context text upload / action** *(stateless resend est.)* | 342.2 KB | **276.2 KB** | **-19.3%** | **-21.9%** | **-58.9%** | **Production hardening highlights (`v0.2.x`):** - **0 disk spills** across 134 consecutive `v0.2.x` MCP calls — strict `≤8.8 KB` UTF-8 inline cap prevents Antigravity's `output.txt` spill-to-disk extra turns. - **+75% effective throughput (`35.1 → 61.5 tok/s`)** and **`>60s` stall turns reduced from `31.2% → 7.4%`** in a same-session before/after `v0.2.1` comparison (99 vs. 374 turns) once multimodal screenshots were isolated out of `>180k`-token main sessions (`0` screenshots loaded in main coding sessions post-upgrade). - **0 lazy-load schema-read turns** — compact schemas are inlined directly in [`rules/AGENTS.md`](rules/AGENTS.md).
Methodology, quota sensitivity & fixed prompt overhead - **Logical action normalization:** One `batch_search` with 5 queries counts as 5 actions, one `apply_edits` touching 6 hunks + `verify` counts as 7 actions, and one built-in `read_file`/`edit_file`/`run_command` counts as 1 action—ensuring apples-to-apples comparison per unit of work rather than raw tool-call counts. - **Quota weighting sensitivity:** Standard weighting (`1.0×` uncached input, `0.1×` cache read, `5.0×` output) yields **-31.5%** on main sessions (**-36.5%** on `≥150k` sessions). Results hold under conservative cache discounts (`1 : 0.25 : 4` → **-25.8%**) and high-output weighting (`1 : 0.1 : 8` → **-29.4%**). - **Fixed prompt overhead:** `rules/AGENTS.md` + `SessionStart` snapshot add **~1.7k tokens** once per session (cached from turn 2 onward, `~170` eq tokens/turn). Avoiding a single redundant turn (`~44k` eq tokens) or blind full-file read pays back this overhead **>20×**.
### Verify on Your Own Transcripts (100% Offline) Measure your own Antigravity sessions locally — nothing ever leaves your machine: ```bash # Summarize all local Antigravity transcripts node dist/benchmark.mjs analyze --local # Analyze only the 10 most recently modified local transcripts node dist/benchmark.mjs analyze --local --recent 10 # Slice sessions since install time and compare With vs. Without agy-fast node dist/benchmark.mjs analyze --local --since 2026-11-19T12:51:00+08:00 --split-usage # Compare two task runs (before vs. after) node dist/benchmark.mjs compare --before ./run-before/transcript.jsonl --after ./run-after/transcript.jsonl ``` ## The 5 MCP Tools | Scenario | Preferred Tool | Why | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | Run ≥2 text, regex, glob, fuzzy, or read-only git queries | **`batch_search`** | 1 call for up to 20 concurrent queries (`<70 ms` local) | | Map unknown large files (`>300` lines) | **`quick_outline`** *(or **`read_slices`**)* | Flat `paths`-only symbol outlines across up to 40 files without full-file dumps | | Read small files (`<300` lines) or known line ranges | Built-in `read_file` | Locally allowlisted (`~7 ms`, `46 KB/call`, 0 remote check) | | Edit ≥2 hunks/files in one turn, or edit + verify | **`apply_edits`** | Atomic or `bestEffort` multi-file edits + optional inline `verify` | | Run ≥2 independent build, lint, test, or diagnostic commands | **`run_checks`** | Concurrent execution with head-tail folded error-focused output | ### 1. `batch_search` — Concurrent Code, Path & Read-Only Git Search - **Up to 20 mixed queries per call:** `text`, `regex`, `glob`, `fuzzy`, and read-only `git` (`status`, `diff`, `log`, `show`, `branch`, `rev-parse`, `ls-files`, `blame`, `shortlog`, `describe`, `tag --list`, `remote -v`), including cross-repo lookups via per-query `path`. - **Precision controls:** Filter by `fileType` (e.g., `typescript`, `python`, `gdscript`) or `glob`, switch `outputMode` (`content` | `files_with_matches` | `count`), enable cross-line `multiline: true` (where `count` reports occurrences per file), use `type: "fuzzy"` for case-insensitive path matching, or pass `sortBy: "mtime"` on `glob` queries for newest-first results. - **Resilient & inline-safe:** Uses `rg` when installed with automatic Node.js fallback, auto-recovers common LLM `glob` mistakes (`|` alternation and bare keywords), and enforces the `≤8.8 KB` UTF-8 cap. ### 2. `apply_edits` — Atomic Multi-Hunk & Multi-File Edits + Verify - **Up to 50 files per call:** Validates every hunk and overlap in memory before touching disk (`0` files modified on error), or pass `bestEffort: true` on larger batches so valid files commit atomically per file while failed files return closest-line / drifted-line snippets for targeted retry. - **Faithful file handling:** Preserves CRLF line endings, file permissions, and symlinks; supports `startLine`/`endLine`, `replaceAll`, `create`/`overwrite`, and `dryRun`. - **Inline `verify`:** Optionally runs a build/typecheck/test command right after writing, stripping noisy logs (e.g., Pino/Bunyan info JSON, Maven footers) so root causes stay within budget. ### 3. `quick_outline` — Flat Multi-Language Symbol Outlines - **Up to 40 files per call** *(10–20 recommended per batch)*: Takes a flat `paths: string[]` array to extract exact `[startLine, endLine]` symbol/section maps for **TypeScript / JavaScript** *(incl. Fastify/Express routes & test blocks)*, **HTML / Vue / Svelte**, **CSS / SCSS / Less**, **Python**, **Godot GDScript (`.gd`)**, **Go**, **Rust**, **Java / Kotlin / C# / Swift / C / C++**, **Shell**, **Markdown**, and **JSON / YAML**—making outline-first exploration effortless before parallel built-in `read_file`. ### 4. `read_slices` — Symbol Outlines + Targeted Line Slices - **Outlines + piggybacked slices:** Supports the same 15-format outlines (with breadth-first water-filling per file) plus optional tiny `[startLine, endLine]` slices in one call under the `≤8.8 KB` UTF-8 budget, while steering bulk range reads (`>150` lines) to parallel built-in `read_file`. ### 5. `run_checks` — Concurrent Build, Lint, Test & Diagnostic Runner - **Up to 12 commands per call:** Executes independent non-interactive shell commands in a bounded worker pool (`concurrency: 1..8`) with per-command timeouts (`1..170 s`, sharing a `170 s` call budget under Antigravity's `180 s` MCP limit), ANSI escape stripping, and transparent Windows unwrapping of trivial `powershell -Command "..."` wrappers around allowlisted binaries (`git`, `npm`, `node`, `rg`, `pytest`, `cargo`, etc.) to skip PowerShell cold-start overhead while leaving PowerShell cmdlets/aliases untouched. - **Head-Tail adaptive output modes:** `compact` (default) collapses passing commands to 1-line summaries and uses **Head-Tail folding** on large failures so both initial root-cause errors and final summary/stack tails survive the `≤8.8 KB` inline cap; `full` preserves stdout for diagnostic or audit scripts with Head-Tail folding when capped.
Example batched MCP calls (JSON payloads) **`batch_search` — 3 heterogeneous queries in one call:** ```json { "queries": [ { "type": "regex", "pattern": "export (async )?function", "fileType": "typescript", "outputMode": "files_with_matches" }, { "type": "fuzzy", "pattern": "mcp server" }, { "type": "git", "pattern": "status --short" } ] } ``` **`apply_edits` — Multi-file edit + inline typecheck in one call:** ```json { "edits": [ { "path": "src/a.ts", "hunks": [{ "target": "oldCall()", "replacement": "newCall()" }] }, { "path": "src/b.ts", "hunks": [{ "target": "v1", "replacement": "v2", "startLine": 10, "endLine": 25 }] } ], "bestEffort": true, "verify": "npm run typecheck" } ```
## Updates, Diagnostics, and Uninstall ### Day-to-Day CLI Reference | Task | Command | | :--- | :--- | | **Health check** *(Node, `rg`, live MCP handshake, `SessionStart` latency, manifest validation)* | `node ~/.gemini/config/plugins/agy-fast/scripts/install.mjs doctor` | | **Check for updates** *(read-only)* | `node ~/.gemini/config/plugins/agy-fast/scripts/install.mjs update --check` | | **Update now** *(stages & runs MCP smoke test before swapping)* | `node ~/.gemini/config/plugins/agy-fast/scripts/install.mjs update` | | **Configure auto-update** *(`auto` \| `notify` \| `off`)* | `node ~/.gemini/config/plugins/agy-fast/scripts/install.mjs config --auto-update notify --interval 24` | | **Switch MCP tool loading** *(`eager` \| `lazy`, preserved across updates)* | `node ~/.gemini/config/plugins/agy-fast/scripts/install.mjs config --tool-loading lazy` | | **Uninstall cleanly** | `node ~/.gemini/config/plugins/agy-fast/scripts/install.mjs uninstall` | > From a local repository clone, `./install.sh ` (macOS/Linux) and `.\install.ps1 ` (Windows) accept the same subcommands (`doctor`, `update`, `config`, `uninstall`). ### Zero-Latency Background Auto-Updater - **0 ms session startup cost:** Every **4 hours**, `SessionStart` spawns a detached background process (`dist/updater.mjs`) *after* emitting the workspace snapshot. - **Verified before swap:** Checks GitHub release tags (`git ls-remote --tags` with GitHub Releases API fallback), clones into an isolated staging directory, runs a **live MCP smoke test**, and atomically replaces runtime files—automatically rejecting broken releases while preserving any user-created `rules/AGENTS.local.md` (add `---\ntrigger: always_on\n---` YAML frontmatter so Antigravity loads it; gitignored for `git clone` installs). - **Safe by design:** Standard copied installs and clean direct `git clone` installs auto-update automatically; `--link` dev symlinks and dirty git repos are **never overwritten** (notify-only). A one-time notice appears in the next new session when an update is applied or available.
Environment variable overrides & applying updates | Environment Variable | Values / Default | Purpose | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `AGY_FAST_AUTO_UPDATE` | `auto` *(default)* \| `notify` \| `off` | Overrides saved auto-update mode | | `AGY_FAST_UPDATE_INTERVAL_HOURS` | `12` *(default; `1..720`)* | Background check interval in hours | | `AGY_FAST_UPDATE_CHANNEL` | `release` *(default)* \| `main` | Track stable semver release tags or `main` | | `AGY_FAST_REPO` | Git URL | Use a custom mirror or fork | | `AGY_FAST_EDITS_FORMAT` | `auto` *(default)* \| `array` \| `string` | Controls `apply_edits.edits` schema (`auto` uses token-saving native arrays on eager-capable CLI ≥1.5.8, Desktop 2.0, IDE, and third-party hosts, and switches to JSON array strings on pre-eager CLI 1.5.0–1.5.7; server always accepts both) | | `AGY_FAST_HOST` | e.g. `cli@1.5.14`, `ide@2.7.0`, `desktop@2.34.0` | Overrides auto-detected Antigravity host surface & version | **Applying updates:** Updated `rules/AGENTS.md` and `dist/session-start.mjs` take effect automatically on the next new session. In Antigravity Desktop 2.0 / IDE, reload or restart the window once to refresh the resident MCP server process.
## Policy Compliance and Safety - **Official interfaces only:** Built exclusively on documented Antigravity extension APIs (`plugin.json`, `mcp_config.json`, `hooks.json`, `rules/AGENTS.md`). - **Non-invasive by design:** Never alters or interferes with Antigravity's native UI, **diff viewer/window**, **modified-files list**, checkpoints, or built-in tools. - **No safety or binary tampering:** Does not patch client binaries, alter authentication, or bypass Antigravity's built-in safety evaluations. - **Zero per-step blocking hooks:** Registers no `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `PreInvocation`, `PostInvocation`, or `Stop` hooks. - **Fail-open startup hook:** On unreadable directories or malformed stdin, `SessionStart` returns `{}` and exits cleanly—never blocking a session. - **Local-first & auditable:** All 5 MCP tools and the benchmark CLI run 100% locally with zero code or transcript uploads; shipped `dist/*.mjs` bundles are unminified ESM so every executed line is directly auditable. ## FAQ ### Does `agy-fast` affect Antigravity's native UI, diff viewer, or modified-files list? No. `agy-fast` runs strictly as a standard local Stdio MCP plugin with a `SessionStart` hook. It never patches the Antigravity client or interferes with the native diff viewer/window, modified-files list, checkpoints, built-in tools, or safety checks. ### Does `agy-fast` save token quota and upload bandwidth in addition to reducing latency? Yes. Across 10 days of sanitized real coding transcripts, batching ~4.9 operations per MCP call reduced LLM turns by **33.7%**, estimated billable token quota by **31.5%** (**36.5%** in `≥150k`-token sessions; **54.0%** in subagents), tool-return upload bytes by **39.7%**, and `>60s` stall turns from **31.2% → 7.4%**. ### Does `agy-fast` replace Antigravity's built-in `read_file` or `edit_file` tools? No — it complements them in a hybrid workflow. Built-in `read_file` is locally allowlisted (`~7 ms`, `46 KB/call`, zero remote check), so `agy-fast` routes small files and known line ranges straight to parallel built-in `read_file`, while handling multi-query searches, symbol outlines, multi-hunk/multi-file edits with inline `verify`, and concurrent checks via MCP. ### Which Antigravity editions and operating systems are supported? `agy-fast` supports **Antigravity CLI (`agy`)**, **Antigravity Desktop 2.0**, and **Antigravity IDE** across **macOS, Linux, and Windows**. It requires **Node.js >= 20** with zero runtime dependencies (optional `ripgrep`/`rg` with automatic pure-Node.js fallback). ### Does `agy-fast` send any code or transcript data to external servers? No. All MCP tools, the `SessionStart` snapshot hook, and the transcript benchmark CLI operate 100% locally. The only optional network request is the background update checker checking public GitHub release tags once every 4 hours, which can be switched to `notify` or disabled completely via `config --auto-update off` or `AGY_FAST_AUTO_UPDATE=off`. ### How do I verify the speedup or uninstall `agy-fast` cleanly? Run `node dist/benchmark.mjs analyze --local --split-usage` to benchmark your own local transcripts completely offline. To remove `agy-fast` at any time, run `node ~/.gemini/config/plugins/agy-fast/scripts/install.mjs uninstall`. ## Development ```bash npm install npm run typecheck # Strict TypeScript check npm run build # Bundle src/*.ts -> dist/*.mjs with esbuild npm test # Run unit, MCP protocol, hook, benchmark, and installer tests npm run bench:stress # Run 12-scenario end-to-end stress & performance benchmark npm run validate # Run `agy plugin validate --strict .` ``` ## MCP Directory ## Star History ## License [MIT](LICENSE)

# Ultimate Open Source Face Recognition SDK

Open Source Face Recognition SDK

A Free, Privacy-Focused Face Recognition Solution for Windows and Linux

Built with deep learning technology, featuring face detection, facial landmarks, feature extraction, and face similarity comparison.

--- ## 🚀 Overview The **Open Source Face Recognition SDK** is a free, privacy-focused solution designed to integrate face recognition capabilities into applications running on Windows and Linux. This is updated version of [faceplugin SDK](https://github.com/Faceplugin-ltd/Open-Source-Face-Recognition-SDK) by further training. ## 🏆 Face Recognition Benchmark: Nataphong-Lab vs FacePlugin We evaluated the face recognition model developed by **Nataphong-Lab** against the original open-source model from **FacePlugin** across five widely recognized face verification benchmark datasets. Nataphong-Lab builds upon FacePlugin's open-source recognition model, applying additional training and model optimization to improve recognition performance. ### 📊 Benchmark Results | Benchmark Dataset | Nataphong-Lab | FacePlugin | Improvement | |:---|---:|---:|---:| | LFW | **98.50%** | 89.20% | **+9.30 pp** | | CFP-FP | **99.10%** | 90.10% | **+9.00 pp** | | AgeDB-30 | **99.20%** | 76.80% | **+22.40 pp** | | CALFW | **98.10%** | 80.30% | **+17.80 pp** | | CPLFW | **96.50%** | 78.90% | **+17.60 pp** | | **Average** | **98.28%** | **83.06%** | **+15.22 pp** | *pp = percentage points.* ### 📈 Key Performance Highlights - **98.28% average benchmark accuracy** across five datasets. - **15.22 percentage-point average improvement** over the FacePlugin baseline. - Consistent improvements across all five evaluated datasets. - Particularly strong performance on AgeDB-30, CALFW, and CPLFW. ### 🔬 Benchmark Datasets | Dataset | Evaluation Focus | |:---|:---| | [LFW](https://vis-www.cs.umass.edu/lfw/) | Unconstrained face verification | | [CFP-FP](https://www.cfpw.org/) | Frontal-to-profile face verification | | [AgeDB-30](https://ibug.doc.ic.ac.uk/resources/agedb/) | Cross-age face verification | | [CALFW](https://github.com/ydwen/calfw) | Cross-age face verification with similar appearance | | [CPLFW](https://github.com/ydwen/cplfw) | Cross-pose face verification | ### 🧪 Evaluation Methodology The comparison uses the face recognition models from the following repositories: - **Nataphong-Lab:** [Open-Source-Face-Recognition-Ultimate](https://github.com/nataphong-lab/Open-Source-Face-Recognition-Ultimate) - **FacePlugin:** [Open-Source-Face-Recognition-SDK](https://github.com/Faceplugin-ltd/Open-Source-Face-Recognition-SDK) For reproducible comparisons, both models should be evaluated using identical dataset splits, image preprocessing, face alignment, verification protocols, and evaluation metrics. **Note:** The figures above are project-reported benchmark results. Independent reproduction and detailed evaluation configurations should be provided alongside the results. Powered by deep learning models, this SDK provides face detection, facial feature extraction, and face similarity comparison through a simple Python interface. **Privacy is a priority:** All biometric processing takes place locally, allowing applications to operate without sending facial data to external servers. ### ✨ Key Features - 🔒 **100% On-Premise Processing:** All face recognition operations run locally. No biometric data needs to leave your device. - 🎯 **High Recognition Accuracy:** Uses deep learning models with additional model training and optimization. - ⚡ **Real-Time Processing:** Supports efficient face detection and recognition workflows. - 🔧 **Easy Integration:** Simple Python APIs for application development. - 🌐 **Cross-Platform:** Supports Windows and Linux. - 💻 **CPU and GPU Support:** Can operate on CPU-only systems, with optional GPU acceleration where supported. - 🆓 **Completely Free:** Open source with no SDK licensing fees. ### 🎯 Current Capabilities - Face detection and bounding box extraction. - Facial landmark detection. - Facial feature embedding generation. - Face similarity comparison. - Multiple face detection within a single image. - Support for common image formats, including JPG, PNG, BMP, and TIFF. --- ## 🛠️ Installation ### Prerequisites Before installing the SDK, make sure you have: - Python 3.9 or higher. - Anaconda or Miniconda (recommended). - Windows or Linux operating system. - Git (recommended). ### 1. Clone the Repository ```bash git clone https://github.com/nataphong-lab/Open-Source-Face-Recognition-Ultimate.git cd Open-Source-Face-Recognition-Ultimate ``` ### 2. Install Python and Necessary Environment Run the following command from the repository directory: ```powershell winget install --id Python.Python.3.9 -e --source winget powershell -Ep Bypass ./install.ps1 ``` ### 3. Create and Activate a Conda Environment ```bash conda create -n facesdk python=3.9 -y conda activate facesdk ``` ### 4. Install Dependencies ```bash pip install -r requirements.txt ``` ### 5. Run the Application ```bash python run.py ``` --- ## 📖 Quick Start ### Basic Usage The following example demonstrates how to initialize the SDK, process an image, and retrieve facial information. ```python from face_recognition_sdk import FaceRecognition # Initialize the SDK face_sdk = FaceRecognition() # Process an image image_path = "path/to/your/image.jpg" face_info = face_sdk.GetImageInfo( image_path, faceMaxCount=10 ) # Display detected faces if face_info: print(f"Detected {len(face_info)} face(s)") for face in face_info: print("Bounding Box:", face["bbox"]) print("Landmarks:", face["landmarks"]) print("Embedding:", face["embedding"]) else: print("No faces detected.") ``` ### Example: Face Comparison Compare two facial images and calculate their similarity score. ```python from face_recognition_sdk import FaceRecognition # Initialize the SDK face_sdk = FaceRecognition() # Input images image1 = "test/1.jpg" image2 = "test/2.png" # Extract facial information faces1 = face_sdk.GetImageInfo(image1, faceMaxCount=1) faces2 = face_sdk.GetImageInfo(image2, faceMaxCount=1) # Compare facial embeddings if faces1 and faces2: feature1 = faces1[0]["embedding"] feature2 = faces2[0]["embedding"] similarity = face_sdk.get_similarity(feature1, feature2) print(f"Similarity: {similarity}%") # Example threshold: 75 is_same_person = similarity >= 75 print(f"Same Person: {is_same_person}") else: print("Unable to detect a face in one or both images.") ``` **Note:** The similarity threshold of 75 is an example configuration. The appropriate threshold should be validated against your application, dataset, and operating conditions. --- ## 🔧 API Reference ### Core Functions #### `FaceRecognition()` Initializes the face recognition SDK. ```python face_sdk = FaceRecognition() ``` #### `GetImageInfo(image_path, faceMaxCount)` Detects faces in an image and extracts facial information. **Parameters:** | Parameter | Type | Description | |---|---|---| | `image_path` | `str` | Path to the input image. | | `faceMaxCount` | `int` | Maximum number of faces to detect. | **Returns:** A list of dictionaries containing facial information: | Field | Description | |---|---| | `bbox` | Face bounding box coordinates. | | `landmarks` | Facial landmark coordinates. | | `embedding` | Extracted facial feature embedding. | #### `get_similarity(feature1, feature2)` Compares two facial feature embeddings and returns a similarity score. **Parameters:** | Parameter | Type | Description | |---|---|---| | `feature1` | `array` | First facial feature embedding. | | `feature2` | `array` | Second facial feature embedding. | **Returns:** A similarity score between 0 and 100, where higher values indicate greater similarity. ### Configuration | Configuration | Value | |---|---| | Default similarity threshold | 75 (example) | | Supported image formats | JPG, PNG, BMP, TIFF | | Face detection | Multiple face detection | | Processing | On-premise | | Supported operating systems | Windows and Linux | --- ## 🎯 Use Cases The SDK can be integrated into a wide range of applications. ### 🔐 Security & Authentication - **Access Control Systems:** Face-based access control and identity verification. - **User Authentication:** Biometric authentication for applications. - **Security Monitoring:** Face detection and recognition workflows. ### 👥 Business Applications - **Time & Attendance:** Automated employee check-in and check-out. - **Customer Analytics:** Face-based customer analysis, subject to applicable privacy requirements. - **Smart Offices:** Visitor identification and management. ### 📱 Mobile & IoT - **Smart Devices:** Face recognition integration for connected devices. - **Application Development:** Biometric functionality for software applications. - **Augmented Reality:** Face detection and facial landmark applications. --- ## 📞 Get in Touch For questions, suggestions, collaboration, or technical support: - **Email:** [nataphong-lab@gmail.com](mailto:nataphong-lab@gmail.com) - **GitHub:** [nataphong-lab](https://github.com/nataphong-lab) ---

# homeport

**一句话：让 Claude、Google、Stripe 这些网站，在你所有设备上都看到同一个“住宅 IP”。**

很多人用机场节点访问 Claude / Google，节点一会儿日本一会儿美国，IP 来回跳，再加上机场 IP 是机房 IP，很容易触发风控：注册要验证、付款失败、身份认证不过、甚至封号。

homeport 做的事情很简单：把这些“敏感网站”单独挑出来，统一走一条固定的**住宅代理**；其他网站照旧走你的机场，速度不受影响。

> 🛒 **还没有住宅 IP？** 看这篇 👉 [便宜静态住宅 IP 购买教程](https://x.com/0xjackkk/status/2117862295397335283)

---

## ⚡ 懒人一键版（推荐小白）

打开 👉 **https://0xkaka.github.io/homeport/**

1. 照着服务商后台，填上住宅代理的地址、端口、用户名、密码；
2. 选你的设备和软件，点「复制」，到软件里粘贴（iPhone 可以直接扫码加节点）；
3. 打开 `ipv4.webshare.io` 看 IP 对不对。

账号密码只在你自己浏览器里处理，不会上传。下面是详细的手动教程，一键版搞不定再看。

---

## 目录

## 1. 原理（看不懂可以跳过）

```
            ┌──────────────── 敏感网站（Claude / Google / Stripe …）────────────────┐
你的设备 ──►│  跳板（你在机场里选的那个节点）──► 🏠住宅出口-勿选（住宅代理）──► 网站 │
            └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
            其他网站 ──► 照常走你的机场
```

- **🏠住宅出口-勿选**：你买的住宅代理。网站最终看到的就是它的 IP。所有设备填同一个，IP 就一致了。
- **跳板**：国内直连住宅代理，握手内容是明文，容易被干扰断线；先经过一个机场节点再连过去就稳了。跳板就是**你平时在机场里选的那个节点**，你切到哪个，住宅代理就经过哪个；跳板换来换去**不影响**最终 IP。
- 另外，Claude 的 IPv6 地址走住宅代理会报错（502），这套规则直接把它拦掉，让设备自动改用 IPv4，你不用管。

## 2. 开始前要准备什么

### ① 一个机场订阅（你现在翻墙用的那个）

已经能正常翻墙就行。**任何机场、任何地区的节点都行**，节点叫什么名字都没关系：住宅代理会经过你在机场里选的那个节点。

### ② 一条静态住宅代理（HTTP 或 SOCKS5）

去住宅代理服务商购买，选的时候注意三点：
（不会买的话先看 👉 [便宜静态住宅 IP 购买教程](https://x.com/0xjackkk/status/2117862295397335283)）

| 要求 | 说明 |
| --- | --- |
| **静态（Static）** | IP 固定不变。别买“动态/轮换（Rotating）”的。 |
| **住宅（Residential / ISP）** | 不要买“机房（Datacenter）”的。 |
| **HTTP 或 SOCKS5，带用户名密码** | 两种都支持。后台写的是哪个就用哪个，不确定先试 HTTP，不通换 SOCKS5。 |

买好后，后台能看到这样四项信息，**抄下来**，后面每台设备都要填同样的：

| 项目 | 举例（假的，别照抄） |
| --- | --- |
| 地址 / Host（Proxy Address，不是 Assigned IP） | `p.webshare.io` |
| 端口 / Port | `80` |
| 用户名 / Username | `abcd1234-1` |
| 密码 / Password | `xyz789` |

> ⚠️ **地址怎么填：**
> - 后台只给了一个 `IP:端口`（比如 `50.2.71.50:443`）：地址就填这个 IP。
> - 后台同时有代理地址和 Assigned IP（比如 Webshare）：**填代理地址，不是 Assigned IP / 出口 IP。** 比如 Webshare 后台一行里同时有 `p.webshare.io`（代理地址）和 `9.x.x.x`（Assigned IP），要填的是 `p.webshare.io`；那个 IP 是最后网站看到的出口，用来核对结果。

> ⭐ **Webshare 用户**：后台代理列表上方的 **Connection Method** 选 **Backbone Connection**，最稳定。别选 **Rotating Proxy Endpoint**，那个 IP 如果有问题，官方会自动换，换了你要去后台手动获取重新配置才行。切好后列表里的 Proxy Address 就是 `p.webshare.io`，用户名带 `-1` 这类后缀，照着填就行。

> 💡 有的服务商给的是一整串，比如 `p.webshare.io:80:abcd1234-1:xyz789`，按冒号拆开就是 地址:端口:用户名:密码。还有一种是 `用户名:密码@地址:端口`。拆开后分别填到一键配置页的四个格子里。

> 💡 **用 SOCKS5 的**：Mac / Windows / 安卓配置里把 `type: http`（或 `type: "http"`）改成 `socks5`；小火箭节点类型选 **Socks5**。一键页上直接选 SOCKS5 就行。

### ③ 对应的客户端

| 设备 | 客户端 | 怎么装 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mac | Clash Party 或 Clash Verge Rev；M 芯片 Mac 也可以用小火箭 | Clash 类去官方 GitHub Releases 下载 `.dmg`；小火箭在美区 App Store |
| Windows | Clash Verge Rev（推荐）或 Clash Party | 去官方 GitHub Releases 下载 `.exe` 安装包 |
| 安卓 | FlClash（版本 ≥ 0.8.85） | 去官方 GitHub Releases 下载 `.apk` |
| iPhone / iPad | Shadowrocket（小火箭） | 美区 App Store 购买 |

先确认客户端里**机场订阅已经导入、能正常翻墙**，再继续下面的步骤。

> 💡 **用 v2rayN 的**：v2rayN 的分流只能选「代理 / 直连 / 拦截」，做不到“Claude 单独走住宅、住宅再经机场跳板”。请改用 Clash Verge Rev，见 [第 4 节](#4-clash-verge-revwindows--mac) 末尾。

## 3. Clash Party（Mac / Windows）

> Mac 版和 Windows 版界面一样。最省事的是用[一键配置页](https://0xkaka.github.io/homeport/)，软件选「Clash Party」，复制生成好的脚本直接粘贴，跳过第 1 步。

Clash Party 用 **JavaScript 覆写**，和 Clash Verge Rev、FlClash 是同一份脚本。

### 第 1 步：准备脚本（用一键页可跳过）

1. 打开 [`flclash/homeport.js`](flclash/homeport.js)，复制全部内容。
2. 把 `const main = (config) => {` 改成 `function main(config, profileName) {`，最后一行 `};` 改成 `}`。
3. 按 [安卓第 2 步](#第-2-步填住宅代理) 把 `HOME` 里的四项改成你自己的住宅代理。

### 第 2 步：新建覆写

1. 打开 Clash Party，点左侧菜单 **「覆写」**。
2. 点右上角 **＋** → **新建 JavaScript**。
3. 把编辑框里原有内容**全部删掉**，粘贴脚本，保存。

### 第 3 步：启用并重启

1. 左侧点 **「订阅管理」**，在你的机场订阅卡片上点 **⋯ → 编辑信息**，找到 **覆写** 一栏，勾选刚才那份覆写，保存。（这一步最容易漏，不勾等于没装。）
2. 左侧点 **「内核设置」**，点那个 **旋转箭头（重启内核）** 按钮。
3. 确认首页的代理模式是 **规则（Rule）**，不是「全局」或「直连」。
4. **系统代理** 保持打开（浏览器靠它走代理）。想让 Claude 桌面版、Claude Code 这类不认系统代理的软件也走，再打开 **虚拟网卡（TUN）**，第一次会要求授权。

> 🪜 **跳板 = 你在机场里选的节点**：平时怎么选节点照旧，选哪个，住宅代理就经过哪个。只是别选 `🏠住宅出口-勿选`。

## 4. Clash Verge Rev（Windows / Mac）

> 最省事：打开[一键配置页](https://0xkaka.github.io/homeport/)，选好设备，软件选「Clash Verge Rev」，复制生成好的脚本直接粘贴。

Clash Verge Rev 用「扩展脚本」，内容和安卓 FlClash 的脚本几乎一样，只是开头那行要写成 `function main(config, profileName) {`。

1. 打开 Clash Verge Rev → 左侧 **「订阅」**，确认机场订阅已导入，并且现在能正常翻墙。
2. 在机场订阅卡片上 **右键 → 「扩展脚本」**（没有这个菜单的话，用订阅页里的「全局扩展脚本」卡片 → 右键 → 编辑文件）。
3. 把编辑框里原有内容**全部删掉**（Ctrl+A / ⌘A 全选），粘贴脚本：
   - 用一键页：直接粘贴生成好的；
   - 手动：复制 [`flclash/homeport.js`](flclash/homeport.js) 的全部内容，把 `const main = (config) => {` 改成 `function main(config, profileName) {`，最后一行 `};` 改成 `}`，再按 [安卓第 2 步](#第-2-步填住宅代理) 填好 `HOME` 里的四项。
4. **保存**。回到「订阅」页，在机场订阅卡片上**点一下**（重新选中一次），让配置重新加载。
5. 左侧 **「代理」**，顶部模式选 **规则**。
6. 左侧 **「设置」** → 打开 **系统代理**。想让 Claude 桌面版、Claude Code 也走，再打开 **虚拟网卡模式（TUN）**，第一次会提示安装服务，点安装（Windows 需要管理员权限）。

> ⚠️ Clash Verge Rev 的默认端口是 **7897**（不是 7890），下文检查和终端设置里的 `7890` 都换成 `7897`（以「设置 → 端口设置」里显示的为准）。

### 我用的是 v2rayN

v2rayN 做不到这种分流（它的路由只能选「代理 / 直连 / 拦截」），换成 Clash Verge Rev：

1. 去 GitHub 搜 `clash-verge-rev`，在 Releases 里下载 Windows 安装包（文件名带 `x64-setup.exe`），安装。
2. 把同一个机场订阅导进去：机场后台一般能直接复制「Clash 订阅」链接；或者在 v2rayN 的「订阅分组 → 订阅分组设置」里复制订阅地址。到 Clash Verge Rev 的「订阅」页粘贴 → 导入。
3. **退出 v2rayN**（两个软件同时开会抢系统代理）。
4. 按上面 1～6 步做。

> 🪜 **跳板 = 你在机场里选的节点**：平时怎么选节点照旧，选哪个，住宅代理就经过哪个。只是别选 `🏠住宅出口-勿选`。

## 5. 安卓：FlClash

> FlClash、Clash Party、Clash Verge Rev 用的是同一份 **JavaScript 脚本**；FlClash 直接用，另外两个要改一下开头那行（见第 3、4 节）。

### 第 1 步：导入脚本

1. 打开 FlClash，底部点 **「工具」** → **「进阶配置」** → **「脚本」**。
2. 点 **＋（添加）**，选 **通过 URL 导入**，粘贴：

   ```
   https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xkaka/homeport/main/flclash/homeport.js
   ```

### 第 2 步：填住宅代理

1. 点开刚导入的脚本进入编辑。
2. 文件开头有这一段：

   ```js
   const HOME = {
     server: "<HOST>",
     port: 0,
     username: "<USERNAME>",
     password: "<PASSWORD>",
   };
   ```

3. 改成你自己的，例如：

   ```js
   const HOME = {
     server: "p.webshare.io",
     port: 80,
     username: "abcd1234-1",
     password: "xyz789",
   };
   ```

   ⚠️ 引号和逗号都要保留，尖括号删掉；`port` 写数字，不加引号，不能是 0。
4. 保存。**以后不要再“从 URL 重新导入”**，否则会被冲回占位符。

### 第 3 步：让脚本生效（这一步最容易漏）

1. 底部点 **「配置」**，在你的机场订阅上点右侧的 **⋮ / 配置按钮**。
2. 进入 **「覆写」** → **「脚本」** → 选中刚才那份脚本。
3. 回到 **「仪表盘」**，关掉再打开连接（或点重启）。

> 只导入脚本、没在订阅里选中，等于没装。

## 6. 小火箭 Shadowrocket（iPhone / iPad / Mac）

小火箭分两部分：**节点**里填账号密码，**模块**里放规则。

> 💻 **Mac 上用小火箭**（只有 M 芯片 Mac 能装）：步骤和 iPhone 一样。区别只有加节点那步——Mac 上没法扫自己屏幕上的码，用一键页的「复制节点链接」，再切到小火箭，一般会自动弹出「添加节点」；没弹就按第 2 步手动填。

> ⚠️ **顺序很重要：先装模块，再加节点。** 整个过程中，首页**选中的节点**一直保持你平时用的机场节点，**不要点选 `🏠住宅出口-勿选`**。
> `🏠住宅出口-勿选` 只给规则用；选中它会让所有流量都走住宅代理，GitHub 等网站可能打不开，模块就下载失败了。

### 第 1 步：添加模块（趁网络正常先装）

1. 底部点 **「配置」** → **「模块」**。
2. 右上角 **＋**，粘贴：

   ```
   https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xkaka/homeport/main/shadowrocket/homeport.module
   ```

3. 点 **下载**，确认模块列表里出现 `homeport` 且开关是打开的。

### 第 2 步：添加住宅节点

1. 首页右上角点 **＋**。
2. **类型** 选 **HTTP**（你的住宅代理是 SOCKS5 的话选 **Socks5**）。
3. 按下面填：

   | 栏位 | 填什么 |
   | --- | --- |
   | 地址 | 代理地址（Proxy Address），如 `p.webshare.io`，**不是出口 IP** |
   | 端口 | 如 `80` |
   | 用户 | 如 `abcd1234-1` |
   | 密码 | 如 `xyz789` |
   | **备注** | **`🏠住宅出口-勿选`**（必须一字不差，带房子图标；名字故意写成“勿选”，提醒大家别在首页点它） |

4. 右上角 **完成**。

> 备注填错，规则就找不到这个节点，所有敏感网站都会连不上。

> 添加完如果小火箭自动选中了 `🏠住宅出口-勿选`，**马上点回你的机场节点**。

### 第 3 步：设置跳板（代理通过）

1. 在首页节点列表里找到 `🏠住宅出口-勿选`，点它右边的 **ⓘ**。
2. 找到 **「代理通过」**，选一个你机场里**稳定的节点**（哪个地区都行）。
3. 保存。

> 不设也能用，但就是手机直连住宅代理，容易断。跳板节点挂了，回来这里换一个就行。

### 第 4 步：切到“配置”模式

1. 回到首页，**全局路由** 选 **「配置」**，并确认选中的是**机场节点**（不是 🏠住宅出口-勿选）。
   - 选「代理」= 所有流量走当前选中节点，规则不生效。
   - 选「直连」= 全部不翻墙。
2. 首页顶部开关打开，连接。

> 模块优先级比订阅配置高，以后更新机场订阅不会把规则冲掉；小火箭的模块也可以放心点更新，因为账号密码在节点里，不在模块里。

## 7. 检查是否成功

**目标：所有设备看到的 IP 一模一样，而且就是你住宅代理的 IP。**

### 手机 / 平板

打开浏览器访问：

```
https://ipv4.webshare.io/
```

页面上只有一行 IP。和住宅代理后台显示的 IP 对一下。

### 电脑

先用浏览器打开 `https://ipv4.webshare.io/` 看一眼（用 Chrome 的先按 [第 8 节](#8-claude-code终端chrome-的额外设置) 关掉 QUIC）。再用终端确认：

**Mac（Clash Party / Clash Verge Rev）**：打开「终端」，粘贴回车：

```bash
curl -x http://127.0.0.1:7890 https://ipv4.webshare.io/
```

**Windows**：打开 PowerShell，粘贴回车（注意是 `curl.exe`，PowerShell 里直接写 `curl` 会报错）：

```powershell
curl.exe -x http://127.0.0.1:7897 https://ipv4.webshare.io/
```

**Mac 上用小火箭**：小火箭是 VPN 模式，终端一般也会走，直接运行 `curl https://ipv4.webshare.io/`。

输出的 IP 应该和手机上一样。

> 端口：Clash Party 默认 `7890`，Clash Verge Rev 默认 `7897`。改过的话，到软件设置里看“混合端口（Mixed Port）”是多少，替换掉。

## 8. Claude Code、终端、Chrome 的额外设置

### Chrome：关闭 QUIC

Chrome 会用 QUIC（基于 UDP）偷偷绕过代理，导致 IP 不一致。Mac 和 Windows 上的 Chrome 都要关。

1. 地址栏输入 `chrome://flags/#enable-quic`，回车。
2. 把 **Experimental QUIC protocol** 改成 **Disabled**。
3. 点右下角 **Relaunch** 重启 Chrome。

### 终端 / Claude Code：手动指定代理

终端里的程序（包括 Claude Code、git、npm）**不会自动走系统代理**。最简单的办法是在代理软件里打开 **TUN / 虚拟网卡**，所有程序都会走；不想开 TUN，就按下面设环境变量。

**Mac：**

1. 终端里运行 `open ~/.zshrc`（没有这个文件就先运行 `touch ~/.zshrc`）。
2. 在文件末尾加上这三行，保存：

   ```zsh
   export http_proxy=http://127.0.0.1:7890
   export https_proxy=http://127.0.0.1:7890
   export all_proxy=socks5://127.0.0.1:7890
   ```

3. 关掉终端重新打开（或运行 `source ~/.zshrc`）。
4. 验证：运行 `curl https://ipv4.webshare.io/`，应显示住宅 IP。

**Windows（PowerShell）**：Clash Verge Rev 端口 7897，Clash Party 为 7890。当前窗口临时生效：

```powershell
$env:HTTP_PROXY="http://127.0.0.1:7897"
$env:HTTPS_PROXY="http://127.0.0.1:7897"
```

长期生效：运行 `setx HTTP_PROXY http://127.0.0.1:7897` 和 `setx HTTPS_PROXY http://127.0.0.1:7897`，然后重开终端。验证用 `curl.exe https://ipv4.webshare.io/`。

## 9. 常见问题

**Q：Claude / Google 全打不开了。**
A：基本是住宅代理没填对。逐项检查：
- 地址、端口、用户名、密码有没有抄错，尖括号删了没；
- `port` 是不是还是 0；
- 小火箭的节点备注是不是正好 `🏠住宅出口-勿选`；
- 住宅代理有没有到期 / 流量用完（去服务商后台看）。

**Q：Clash Party / Clash Verge Rev / FlClash 报错，配置加载失败。**
A：
- 手动改脚本时把引号、逗号弄丢了。最稳的办法：回[一键配置页](https://0xkaka.github.io/homeport/)重新生成一份，整份覆盖粘贴。
- Clash Party / Clash Verge Rev 忘了把开头改成 `function main(config, profileName) {`（一键页生成的已经改好）。

**Q：跳板是哪个节点？对名字、地区有要求吗？**
A：跳板就是你在机场里选的那个节点（脚本会自动找到机场的主选择组，比如「🚀 节点选择」）。你切到哪个，住宅代理就经过哪个。没有地区要求，香港、日本、美国、欧洲都行；网站最终看到的永远是住宅 IP。
- 主选择组里**别选 `🏠住宅出口-勿选`**，也别选「DIRECT / 直连」（那样住宅代理会变成国内直连，容易断）。
- 少数订阅找不到主选择组，脚本会自动建一个隐藏的 `HP_Relay`，从机场全部节点里测速选最快的。

**Q：页面能打开，但时不时断线 / 很慢。**
A：多半是跳板节点质量差。
- 电脑 / 安卓：在机场里换一个更稳的节点就行，住宅代理会跟着换跳板。
- 小火箭：回到 `🏠住宅出口-勿选` 的 ⓘ →「代理通过」换一个节点。

**Q：所有跳板都挂了，想先凑合用。**
A：
- Clash Party / Clash Verge Rev / 安卓：脚本里把 `const FORCE_RELAY = "";` 改成 `const FORCE_RELAY = "DIRECT";`。
- 小火箭：「代理通过」改成不选。

代价是直连住宅代理，可能会被干扰断线。

**Q：手机和电脑的 IP 不一样。**
A：
- 每台设备填的是不是同一条住宅代理；
- 小火箭全局路由是不是「配置」，Clash 是不是「规则」模式；
- 电脑上 Chrome 的 QUIC 关了没；
- 电脑上的 Clash 系统代理开了没。

**Q：规则更新了，我要怎么更新？**
A：
- 小火箭：「配置」→「模块」→ 左滑 homeport → 更新。账号在节点里，不受影响。
- 其他：最省事是回[一键配置页](https://0xkaka.github.io/homeport/)重新生成一份，覆盖粘贴。手动改的话先把四个值记好，更新（或重新导入）后再填一遍。

---

## 10. 哪些网站会走住宅出口

| 类别 | 域名 / 规则 |
| --- | --- |
| Claude / Anthropic | `claude.ai` `claude.com` `clau.de` `anthropic.com` `claudeusercontent.com` `claudemcpcontent.com` `modelcontextprotocol.io`，含关键词 `anthropic` `claude`，以及 Anthropic 的 IP 段和 ASN |
| 监控 / 风控 | `sentry.io` `datadoghq.com`（含 `browser-intake`）`growthbook.io` `usefathom.com` `segment.io` `siftscience.com` `intercom.io` `intercomcdn.com` |
| 人机验证 | `hcaptcha.com` `challenges.cloudflare.com` `recaptcha.net` |
| 支付 / 身份认证 | `stripe.com` `stripe.network` `stripecdn.com` `withpersona.com` |
| Google | `google.com` `googleapis.com` `gstatic.com` `googleusercontent.com` `gmail.com` |
| 安卓 App（仅 FlClash） | Claude App、Google Play、Google Wallet |
| IP 检测 | `webshare.io` `ipinfo.io` |
| 拦截 | Anthropic IPv6 `2607:6bc0::/48` `2607:6bc0:11::/48` |

不在表里的网站，照常走你的机场。

---

## 11. 给维护者：修改规则

两份文件要**同步修改**（Clash Party / Clash Verge Rev / FlClash 共用第一份；一键页的规则在 `index.html` 的 `GROUPS` 里，也要一起改）：

| 文件 | 改哪里 |
| --- | --- |
| `flclash/homeport.js` | `SUFFIX` 数组里加 `"example.com",` |
| `shadowrocket/homeport.module` | `[Rule]` 下面加一行 `DOMAIN-SUFFIX,example.com,🏠住宅出口-勿选` |

改完运行自检（会用几种订阅样例实际跑脚本，检查跳板选得对不对、两份规则是否一致）：

```bash
python3 scripts/check.py
```

推送到 GitHub 后，Actions 也会自动跑一遍。
